occurrences.passage_locator: THE BAMBOO-CUTTER AND THE MOON-CHILD / THE GOBLIN OF ADACHIGAHARA / THE SAGACIOUS MONKEY AND THE BOAR / THE HAPPY HUNTER AND THE SKILLFUL FISHER; lines 4436-4526
occurrences.motif_label: Rival brothers, usurpation, and restoration of rule
occurrences.basis: The Skillful Fisher usurps his brother's position, attempts to kill him, then promises to restore his rights and acknowledge him as Lord of all Japan.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The Skillful Fisher had used the lost hook as an excuse to drive out his brother, usurped his place as ruler, and became powerful and rich; he is surprised by the Happy Hunter's return.
The Skillful Fisher only pretends forgiveness, hates his brother, plans to kill him, and follows him in the rice fields with a dagger; the Happy Hunter decides to use the tide jewels.
The Skillful Fisher, frightened and impressed, humbles himself, asks forgiveness, promises to restore his brother's rights, and swears to bow before him as Lord of all Japan.
The Happy Hunter rules without family strife, Japan has peace for a long time, and he prizes the Jewels of the Flow and Ebb of the Tide given by Ryn Jin, the Dragon King of the Sea.

occurrences.source_title: Japanese Fairy Tales
occurrences.passage_locator: PREFACE / JAPANESE FAIRY TALES / MY LORD BAG OF RICE / THE TONGUE-CUT SPARROW; lines 509-612
occurrences.motif_label: journey out and return home with a gift
occurrences.basis: The old man travels to find the sparrow, enters her hidden home in the bamboo grove, receives a gift, and returns home.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The old man reaches a bamboo wood, finds his sparrow waiting, hears her speak, sees that a new tongue has grown, and realizes she is a fairy rather than a common bird.
The sparrow leads the old man to a beautiful house in the bamboo grove, furnished with fine mats, silk and crape cushions, vases, lacquer boxes, and tokonoma alcoves.

The old man says he must return home; the Lady Sparrow offers him one of two boxes, large or small, and he chooses the smaller because he is too old and feeble to carry the larger one. The sparrows help him leave with it.
The old man comes home late, finds his wife angry, tells her of his visit to the sparrow’s house, and they sit down to open the box.

occurrences.source_title: Japanese Fairy Tales
occurrences.passage_locator: THE JELLY FISH AND THE MONKEY / THE QUARREL OF THE MONKEY AND THE CRAB / THE WHITE HARE AND THE CROCODILES / THE STORY OF PRINCE YAMATO TAKE; lines 5813-5924
occurrences.motif_label: return of the victorious hero to royal honor
occurrences.basis: After defeating the King's enemies, Yamato Take returns to the capital and receives praise, feast, gifts, and increased affection from the King.

evidence.quote_or_summary: When Yamato Take returns to the capital, the King praises him, holds a palace feast, gives rare gifts, and loves him more than ever.

occurrences.source_title: Japanese Fairy Tales
occurrences.passage_locator: THE JELLY FISH AND THE MONKEY / THE QUARREL OF THE MONKEY AND THE CRAB / THE WHITE HARE AND THE CROCODILES / THE STORY OF PRINCE YAMATO TAKE; lines 6128-6233
occurrences.motif_label: return to sacred shrine and thanksgiving to ancestral goddess
occurrences.basis: After recovery, Yamato Take returns to Ise, is welcomed by his aunt the priestess, and thanks are offered to the ancestral Sun Goddess Amaterasu for his preservation.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Yamato Take returns to the temples of Ise; his aunt, the shrine priestess, welcomes him, hears his account, praises him, and gives thanks to the ancestral Sun Goddess Amaterasu for his preservation.

occurrences.source_title: Japanese Fairy Tales
occurrences.passage_locator: THE QUARREL OF THE MONKEY AND THE CRAB / THE WHITE HARE AND THE CROCODILES / THE STORY OF PRINCE YAMATO TAKE / MOMOTARO, OR THE STORY OF THE SON OF A PEACH; lines 6647-6752
occurrences.motif_label: Triumphant return with treasure and restored captives
occurrences.basis: Momotaro returns home with plunder and the captive chief devil, restores abducted people to their homes, and brings prosperity to the old couple.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The dog and pheasant carry home the plunder, and Momotaro returns triumphantly with the devil chief as a captive.
The damsels and other enslaved captives are taken safely home, and the country celebrates Momotaro as the hero who freed it from the robber devils.
The old couple rejoices, and Momotaro’s treasure lets them live in peace and plenty to the end of their days.

occurrences.source_title: Japanese Fairy Tales
occurrences.passage_locator: JAPANESE FAIRY TALES / MY LORD BAG OF RICE / THE TONGUE-CUT SPARROW / THE STORY OF URASHIMA TARO, THE FISHER LAD; lines 983-1099
occurrences.motif_label: Remembering home and returning from an otherworld
occurrences.basis: After forgetting his home and parents, Urashima remembers them and insists on returning to his own land.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Urashima's happiness makes him forget home, parents, and country for three days; then he remembers he does not belong there and must return to his old father and mother.
Urashima tells Otohime Sama he must go back to his old parents; she weeps and asks him to stay another day, but he insists and says he will return.
Urashima says goodbye, finds a large tortoise waiting at the seashore, rides it over the shining sea into the East, and looks toward his own land.

occurrences.source_title: Jataka tales
occurrences.passage_locator: THE QUARREL OF THE QUAILS / THE MEASURE OF RICE / THE FOOLISH, TIMID RABBIT / THE WISE AND THE FOOLISH MERCHANT; lines 1075-1086
occurrences.motif_label: Successful journey and return with profit
occurrences.basis: The merchant reaches the city across the desert, sells the goods at a profit, and returns with his company to his own city.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Early the next day, the merchant takes the best wagons left by the foolish merchant and goes safely to the city across the desert.
At the city he sells all the goods at a profit and returns with his company to his own city.

occurrences.source_title: Jataka tales
occurrences.passage_locator: THE WISE AND THE FOOLISH MERCHANT / THE ELEPHANT GIRLY-FACE / THE BANYAN DEER / THE PRINCES AND THE WATER-SPRITE; lines 1228-1339
occurrences.motif_label: restored royal order with shared rule
occurrences.basis: After forest exile and the pond ordeal, the brothers return to the palace, the eldest is made king, and he includes his brothers in rule.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The three princes live in the forest until the king dies, then return to the palace; the eldest is made king, has his brothers rule with him, and builds a home for the water-sprite in the palace grounds.

occurrences.source_title: More Jataka Tales
occurrences.passage_locator: XVIII / THE WISE GOAT AND THE WOLF / PRINCE WICKED AND THE GRATEFUL ANIMALS / BEAUTY AND BROWNIE; lines 1582-1626
occurrences.motif_label: seasonal departure and safe return
occurrences.basis: The deer are instructed to leave the forest for the high hills during the crop season and return after the crops are cut.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The father says he, the mother, and older deer will stay in the forest, while Beauty and Brownie must lead their herds to the high hills until the crops are cut.
Beauty travels at night, avoids villages, brings his herd safely to the high hills, and loses no deer.
When crops are cut, the deer return; Beauty brings all his herd back, while Brownie again travels by day past villages and reaches the forest with only a few deer left.

occurrences.source_title: More Jataka Tales
occurrences.passage_locator: XX BEAUTY AND BROWNIE / XXI THE ELEPHANT AND THE DOG / THE GIRL MONKEY AND THE STRING OF PEARLS / THE THREE FISHES; lines 264-305
occurrences.motif_label: return from dangerous place to safe home
occurrences.basis: After the trap and rescue, all three fishes go back to their old home and live safely.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The rescued fishes say that Very-Thoughtful saved their lives and that they are now willing to go back to the wild country.
All three fishes return to their old home and live safely ever after.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: ALCMAEON AND THE NECKLACE. / THE HERACLIDAE. / THE SIEGE OF TROY. / RETURN OF THE GREEKS FROM TROY.; lines 10012-10108
occurrences.motif_label: Cursed return voyage
occurrences.basis: After Odysseus reveals his name, Polyphemus asks Poseidon to make his return long, late, unhappy, and desolate, with ships and companions destroyed.

evidence.quote_or_summary: After boarding the ship, Odysseus reveals his name and mocks Polyphemus; Polyphemus hurls a rock and asks Poseidon to curse Odysseus' voyage and return.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: ALCMAEON AND THE NECKLACE. / THE HERACLIDAE. / THE SIEGE OF TROY. / RETURN OF THE GREEKS FROM TROY.; lines 10110-10199
occurrences.motif_label: return home delayed by supernatural or hostile obstacles
occurrences.basis: The voyagers come within sight of Ithaca but are driven back by released winds, rejected by Aeolus, attacked by cannibal giants, and driven onward to Aeaea.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Near Ithaca, while Odysseus sleeps, his comrades open the bag thinking it may hold treasure; adverse winds rush out, drive them back to Aeolus, and Aeolus reproaches and dismisses them.
Odysseus sends a herald and two companions for provisions; they reach the Laestrygones, a race of fierce gigantic cannibals ruled by Antiphates, who kills the herald.
Antiphates and the other giants pursue the fugitives, hurl huge rocks, sink eleven ships with all hands, and only Odysseus' own ship escapes.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: ALCMAEON AND THE NECKLACE. / THE HERACLIDAE. / THE SIEGE OF TROY. / RETURN OF THE GREEKS FROM TROY.; lines 10201-10297
occurrences.motif_label: dead kin reveal the cost of the hero's absence
occurrences.basis: Anticlea tells Odysseus she died of grief at his absence and that Laertes suffers while awaiting his return.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Other shades drink and speak: Odysseus recognizes Anticlea, learns she died of grief and that Laertes longs for his return, converses with Agamemnon, Patroclus, and Achilles, and is refused by Ajax.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: ALCMAEON AND THE NECKLACE. / THE HERACLIDAE. / THE SIEGE OF TROY. / RETURN OF THE GREEKS FROM TROY.; lines 10201-10297
occurrences.motif_label: voyage home threatened by monsters and divine prohibitions
occurrences.basis: Tiresias and Circe warn Odysseus of dangers during his homeward voyage; Scylla kills six men, and Helios' sacred herds are forbidden to the crew.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Tiresias comes with a golden staff, drinks the sacrifice, reveals Odysseus' future fate, and warns him how to avoid dangers on the voyage and after returning to Ithaca.
As Odysseus steers beneath the great rock near Scylla and Charybdis, Scylla swoops down and seizes six crewmen from the deck.

The ship reaches Trinacria, where Helios pastures sacred flocks and herds; Odysseus remembers Tiresias' warning to avoid the island, but the mutinous crew insists on landing, and he makes them swear not to touch the herds.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: ALCMAEON AND THE NECKLACE. / THE HERACLIDAE. / THE SIEGE OF TROY. / RETURN OF THE GREEKS FROM TROY.; lines 10299-10392
occurrences.motif_label: Divine intercession secures the hero's departure
occurrences.basis: Athene intercedes with Zeus, Hermes conveys the order, and Calypso equips Odysseus to depart on a raft toward home.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Athene intercedes with Zeus; Zeus sends Hermes to command Calypso to release Odysseus and provide transport; Calypso obeys, instructs him in raft-building, weaves the sails, and he departs alone.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: ALCMAEON AND THE NECKLACE. / THE HERACLIDAE. / THE SIEGE OF TROY. / RETURN OF THE GREEKS FROM TROY.; lines 10299-10392
occurrences.motif_label: Perilous sea return with repeated wrecks and divine aid
occurrences.basis: Odysseus repeatedly tries to resume his homeward voyage, survives storms and wrecks, receives aid from Leucothea and hospitality from Nausicaa and the Phaeacian rulers.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Zeus promises vengeance; after seven days of feasting, the crew sail, a storm and lightning destroy the ship, all the crew drown except Odysseus, who floats on a mast for nine days and reaches Ogygia after escaping Charybdis.

Odysseus pilots the raft for seventeen days by Calypso's directions and the stars; on the eighteenth day he sights the Phaeacian coast, but Poseidon sends a tempest that swamps the raft, leaving him clinging to wreckage.
After two days and nights amid angry waves, Leucothea aids Odysseus, and he is cast ashore on Scheria, where he hides in a thicket and sleeps on dried leaves.

Odysseus wakes and emerges; the attendants flee, but Nausicaa pities him, hears his account, calls the attendants back, orders food, drink, and clothing, and later admires him after Athene enhances his appearance, inviting him to her father's palace.
Alcinous and Arete receive Odysseus with magnificent hospitality, and he recounts his voyage, adventures, and escapes since leaving Ilion.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: ALCMAEON AND THE NECKLACE. / THE HERACLIDAE. / THE SIEGE OF TROY. / RETURN OF THE GREEKS FROM TROY.; lines 10394-10485
occurrences.motif_label: Return of the long-absent hero to his homeland
occurrences.basis: Odysseus reaches Ithaca after twenty years away, rejoices on touching his native land, and re-enters his household under concealment.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Odysseus sleeps deeply on the Phaeacian vessel; the sailors land him at Ithaca and place him under an olive-tree.

Athene hides Odysseus in a cloud, appears as a shepherd, tells him he is in Ithaca, reports on his family and the suitors, describes Penelope's weaving stratagem, and Odysseus kisses his native ground.

Athene urges Odysseus to reveal himself to Telemachus, restores his royal appearance, and father and son embrace; they plan secrecy and a bow contest, then Odysseus resumes beggar form and is recognized by Argo, who dies.
In the palace the suitors mock Odysseus in beggar form; Antinous orders him away, but Penelope receives him kindly and hears his false Cretan report about Odysseus' return.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: ALCMAEON AND THE NECKLACE. / THE HERACLIDAE. / THE SIEGE OF TROY. / RETURN OF THE GREEKS FROM TROY.; lines 10487-10546
occurrences.motif_label: Return of the long-absent hero
occurrences.basis: Odysseus returns after long absence, is not immediately recognized, reunites with wife and father, and resumes stable rule.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Penelope hears of Odysseus' return but refuses to recognize her husband in the aged beggar.
Penelope recognizes Odysseus, and the long-separated husband and wife have an affectionate reunion.
Odysseus reveals himself to Laertes; Laertes rejoices, resumes regal robes, and thanks the gods.
The suitors' relatives rebel and pursue Odysseus, but after brief conflict peace is negotiated and his subjects are reconciled to him.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: CERES. / APHRODITE (VENUS). / VENUS. / HELIOS (SOL).; lines 1985-2069
occurrences.motif_label: solar departure and return
occurrences.basis: Helios rises in the east, traverses the sky, descends westward, and in later poetry returns east by a winged vessel.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Helios, son of Hyperion and Theia, rises in the east preceded by Eos, drives a gold fiery chariot with fire-breathing steeds, descends toward the sea, is followed by Selene, and rests on a couch prepared by sea-nymphs.
The passage notes no Homeric or Hesiodic explanation of Helios' return, but later poets invent a winged boat or cup made by Hephaestus to carry him from west to east.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: VENUS. / HELIOS (SOL). / EOS (AURORA). / PHOEBUS-APOLLO.; lines 2441-2527
occurrences.motif_label: hero descends to tomb and wrests beloved from Death
occurrences.basis: Heracles descends into the tomb, restrains Death, and secures Alcestis' restoration to her family.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Heracles arrives at Admetus' palace, learns of Alcestis' death, descends into the tomb, and holds Death until he promises to restore Alcestis to her family.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: VENUS. / HELIOS (SOL). / EOS (AURORA). / PHOEBUS-APOLLO.; lines 2598-2664
occurrences.motif_label: conditional return from the underworld failed by a backward look
occurrences.basis: Eurydice's release depends on Orpheus not looking at her before reaching the upper world; he looks back and loses her.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Before Aides and Persephone, Orpheus pleads through song; they consent to release Eurydice if he does not look at her until reaching the upper world, but he looks back near the boundary and loses her forever.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: NEW YORK: / PREFACE. / E. M. BERENS. / CONTENTS.; lines 282-303
occurrences.motif_label: return from Troy
occurrences.basis: The table of contents includes the title “Return of the Greeks from Troy.”

evidence.quote_or_summary: “RETURN OF THE GREEKS FROM TROY,      304”

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: ARTEMIS (DIANA). / ARCADIAN ARTEMIS. / EPHESIAN ARTEMIS. / BRAURONIAN ARTEMIS.; lines 2976-3057
occurrences.motif_label: escape from a land of ritual danger
occurrences.basis: Iphigenia, long exiled in Taurica and serving in a violent cult, escapes with Orestes and Pylades after recognizing her brother.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Iphigenia pleads for life and is bound to the altar; before the knife falls, Artemis replaces her with a deer, carries her in a cloud to Taurica, and makes her priestess in the temple.
Pylades sees that the letter is addressed to Orestes; Iphigenia and Orestes recognize each other, and she escapes with Orestes and Pylades from Taurica.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: VICTORIA. / HERMES (MERCURY). / MERCURY. / DIONYSUS (BACCHUS).; lines 3954-4041
occurrences.motif_label: departure, expedition, and return
occurrences.basis: Dionysus travels through eastern regions and later returns to Greece from his Eastern expedition.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Dionysus leads men, women, fauns, and satyrs bearing Thyrsi and instruments; seated in a panther-drawn chariot, he progresses through Syria, Egypt, Arabia, India, and other regions, conquering, founding cities, and civilizing.

On return to Greece, Dionysus encounters Lycurgus, who drives the nymphs from Nysa; Dionysus leaps into the sea and is received by Thetis; Lycurgus is punished with madness and kills Dryas, mistaking him for a vine.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: FORTUNA. / ANANKE (NECESSITAS). / MOMUS. / EROS (CUPID, AMOR) AND PSYCHE.; lines 4825-4914
occurrences.motif_label: Lost divine beloved sought through wandering and trials
occurrences.basis: After Eros departs, Psyche wanders over the world searching for him and undergoes hard tasks with hidden aid.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Psyche approaches Eros at night with lamp and dagger, sees his beautiful form, accidentally drops burning oil on him, and Eros wakes, reproaches her, spreads his wings, and leaves.
Psyche wanders over the world searching for Eros, appeals to Aphrodite, receives hard tasks, and is aided by invisible beneficent beings sent by Eros.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: ANANKE (NECESSITAS). / MOMUS. / EROS (CUPID, AMOR) AND PSYCHE. / HYMEN.; lines 4964-4987
occurrences.motif_label: journey to festival interrupted by abduction and return
occurrences.basis: The maidens depart from Athens toward Eleusis for a festival, are abducted to an island, and are eventually returned safely to Athens.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Hymen disguises himself as a girl and joins maidens, including his beloved, traveling from Athens to Eleusis for a festival of Demeter.
Pirates surprise the travelers, carry them to a desert island, drink deeply, and fall into heavy sleep.
After the parents agree, Hymen returns to the island, brings the maidens safely back to Athens, marries his beloved, and their happy union makes his name synonymous with conjugal felicity.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: CADMUS. / PERSEUS. / THE ARGONAUTS. / STORY OF THE GOLDEN FLEECE.; lines 7145-7238
occurrences.motif_label: Lost kin recognized and restored
occurrences.basis: Chalciope recognizes the sons of Phryxus, whom she had mourned as dead, when they return with Jason's party.

evidence.quote_or_summary: At the palace grounds, Chalciope recognizes the youths as her sons whom she had mourned as dead, while Medea is struck by Jason's noble and manly form.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: CADMUS. / PERSEUS. / THE ARGONAUTS. / STORY OF THE GOLDEN FLEECE.; lines 7432-7522
occurrences.motif_label: guided quest-return after ordeal
occurrences.basis: The Argonauts follow a supernatural sea-horse, carry the Argo through a desert ordeal, reach the sea, and eventually return to Iolcus with the Golden Fleece.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A gigantic hippocamp approaches; Jason reports the Libyan prophetess' words; the Argonauts carry the Argo, follow the sea-horse through the desert for twelve days, reach the sea, sacrifice to the gods, and launch the ship again.
After storm and darkness, the Argonauts reach Iolcus; their adventures are admired; the Argo is consecrated to Poseidon, preserved for generations, and later placed in heaven as a constellation.
Jason arrives at Iolcus with Medea and the Golden Fleece, but Pelias refuses to fulfil his compact and declines to abdicate the throne.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: THE ARGONAUTS. / STORY OF THE GOLDEN FLEECE. / PELOPS. / HERACLES (HERCULES).; lines 8170-8264
occurrences.motif_label: return of heroic agency after bondage
occurrences.basis: When the term of bondage expires, Heracles leaves Omphale's palace and resumes independent action and vengeance.

evidence.quote_or_summary: When the term of bondage expires, Heracles leaves Omphale's palace and resolves to take revenge against Laomedon and Augeas.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: PELOPS. / HERACLES (HERCULES). / BELLEROPHON. / THESEUS.; lines 8505-8590
occurrences.motif_label: Return signal misunderstood through forgotten sails
occurrences.basis: Theseus promises white sails for a safe return but forgets to change the black sails, leading Aegeus to think he is dead.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The vessel normally bears black sails on the tribute voyage; Theseus promises to hoist white sails if he returns safely.
Grieving the loss of Ariadne, Theseus and his companions forget the black sails; Aegeus sees them, believes Theseus dead, and throws himself into the sea.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: PELOPS. / HERACLES (HERCULES). / BELLEROPHON. / THESEUS.; lines 8683-8725
occurrences.motif_label: Rescue from underworld captivity
occurrences.basis: Heracles releases Theseus from imprisonment in Hades, permitting his return to the world above.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Heracles passes by while searching for Cerberus, releases Theseus, and leaves Pirithoeus to perpetual punishment under divine injunction.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: PELOPS. / HERACLES (HERCULES). / BELLEROPHON. / THESEUS.; lines 8683-8725
occurrences.motif_label: Posthumous return of heroic remains and foundation of honor shrine
occurrences.basis: By the Delphic oracle's command, Theseus' remains are brought back to Athens and a temple is erected in his honor.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Centuries later, by command of the Delphic oracle, Cimon brings Theseus' remains to Athens, where a temple is erected in his honor.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: THE SEVEN AGAINST THEBES. / THE EPIGONI. / ALCMAEON AND THE NECKLACE. / THE HERACLIDAE.; lines 9109-9206
occurrences.motif_label: Repeated failed return to ancestral land
occurrences.basis: Successive descendants of Heracles repeatedly attempt to enter or reclaim the Peloponnesus but are forced back or killed.

evidence.quote_or_summary: After twelve months in the Peloponnesus, a pestilence spreads across the peninsula and forces the Heraclidae to return to Attica.

Hyllus consults Delphi and is told to wait for the third fruit; taking this as the third summer, he invades, meets Atreus' opposition, proposes single combat, and is killed by Echemon, after which the Heraclidae withdraw for fifty years.
Cleodaeus, son of Hyllus, invades the Peloponnesus after the appointed time but dies there with all his forces.
Aristomachus consults an oracle promising victory by way of the defile; the Heraclidae set out again but are defeated, and Aristomachus dies in battle.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: THE EPIGONI. / ALCMAEON AND THE NECKLACE. / THE HERACLIDAE. / THE SIEGE OF TROY.; lines 9514-9591
occurrences.motif_label: Embassy offers restitution to restore the absent hero
occurrences.basis: Agamemnon offers Briseis, marriage, and towns to persuade Achilles to help the Greeks, but Achilles refuses.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Agamemnon sends distinguished chiefs to ask Achilles for aid, offering Briseis, marriage to his daughter, and seven towns, but Achilles refuses.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: THE EPIGONI. / ALCMAEON AND THE NECKLACE. / THE HERACLIDAE. / THE SIEGE OF TROY.; lines 9514-9591
occurrences.motif_label: Hero returns to battle for vengeance
occurrences.basis: After Patroclus' death, Achilles abandons his apathy, reconciles with Agamemnon, and rejoins the Greek army.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Achilles grieves over Patroclus and vows that funeral rites will wait until he has slain Hector and captured twelve Trojans for immolation on the funeral pyre.
Achilles returns from apathy, reconciles with Agamemnon, rejoins the Greek army, and receives new armor forged by Hephaestus at Thetis' request.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: THE EPIGONI. / ALCMAEON AND THE NECKLACE. / THE HERACLIDAE. / THE SIEGE OF TROY.; lines 9593-9685
occurrences.motif_label: Hero withdraws from army and is persuaded to return
occurrences.basis: Achilles leaves the Greek army for Lesbos after a dispute and is persuaded by Odysseus to return.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Diomedes claims compensation for Thersites' death, Agamemnon does not intervene, Achilles resents the implied condemnation and sails to Lesbos, and Odysseus persuades him to return.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: THE EPIGONI. / ALCMAEON AND THE NECKLACE. / THE HERACLIDAE. / THE SIEGE OF TROY.; lines 9869-9911
occurrences.motif_label: reconciliation with recovered spouse after war
occurrences.basis: Menelaus seeks Helen in the palace, is reconciled with her, and she accompanies him on the voyage home.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Menelaus finds Helen, who is immortal and still beautiful; they reconcile and sail home. Andromache, Cassandra, and Hecuba are assigned to or captured by Greek victors.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome
occurrences.passage_locator: ALCMAEON AND THE NECKLACE. / THE HERACLIDAE. / THE SIEGE OF TROY. / RETURN OF THE GREEKS FROM TROY.; lines 9913-10010
occurrences.motif_label: dangerous return after sacrilege
occurrences.basis: The passage explicitly links the Greeks' troubled homeward voyages to divine wrath after desecration and cruelty at Troy.

evidence.locator: lines 9913-10010; RETURN OF THE GREEKS FROM TROY, opening paragraph
evidence.quote_or_summary: During the sack of Troy the Greeks commit desecration and cruelty; the gods' wrath makes their homeward voyage full of dangers and deaths.

occurrences.source_title: Myths and Legends of Ancient Greece and Rome

occurrences.basis: Agamemnon's safe voyage ends in death when his wife and her ally murder him on his arrival at Mycenae.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Clytemnestra, seeking revenge for Iphigenia's sacrifice, allies with Aegisthus; despite Cassandra's warnings, Agamemnon trusts her welcome, and Aegisthus kills him at her signal.

occurrences.motif_label: avenging son kills parental murderer
occurrences.basis: Orestes returns in disguise to Mycenae and kills Clytemnestra and Aegisthus to avenge Agamemnon.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Orestes grows intent on avenging his father, returns in disguise with Pylades, and sends a messenger falsely reporting Orestes' death in a chariot-race.
Orestes reveals himself to the grieving Electra, learns of her treatment and his mother's joy at his supposed death, then kills Clytemnestra and Aegisthus.

occurrences.motif_label: forgetfulness of home through enchanted food
occurrences.basis: The lotus causes oblivion of home and country and threatens the companions' return until Odysseus forces them back to the ships.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Storms drive Odysseus's fleet to the land of the lotus-eaters; the honey-sweet lotus causes oblivion of home, and Odysseus must force affected companions back to the ships.

occurrences.motif_label: divine absence, usurpation, and restorative return
occurrences.basis: Odin is absent from Asgard; Vili and Ve usurp his place; they vanish when Odin returns.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Odin is absent so long that the gods fear he will not return; Vili and Ve usurp his power and throne and are said to take Frigga; the passage cites Sæmund's Edda.
On Odin's return the usurpers vanish; the passage connects this to northern yearly festivals and May Day rejoicings, including the Swedish May Ride and English May Day customs.

occurrences.passage_locator: LIST OF ILLUSTRATIONS / INTRODUCTION / CHAPTER I: THE BEGINNING / CHAPTER II: ODIN; lines 1709-1827
occurrences.motif_label: ritual self-wounding before return to divine homeland
occurrences.basis: As death approaches, Odin wounds himself nine times with a spear and announces return to Asgard, where he will await followers for feasting, drinking, and fighting.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Near death, the semi-historical Odin assembles followers, cuts himself nine times in the breast with his spear, calls this carving Geir odds, and says he will return to Asgard to await them.

occurrences.source_title: Myths of the Norsemen: From the Eddas and Sagas
occurrences.passage_locator: CHAPTER IV: THOR / CHAPTER V: TYR / CHAPTER VI: BRAGI / CHAPTER VII: IDUN; lines 4135-4274
occurrences.motif_label: recovery of an abducted or absent goddess
occurrences.basis: Idun is absent from Asgard, held by Thiassi, and brought back by Loki to the gods.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Loki is threatened by the gods, promises to restore Idun, borrows Freya's falcon plumage, flies to Thrym-heim, finds Idun mourning exile from Asgard and Bragi, changes her into a nut or swallow, and carries her back.

The gods wait on Asgard's ramparts with fuel ready; Thiassi returns, sees Idun has been taken by a falcon, dons eagle plumes, pursues Loki, and is brought down by the gods' flames and smoke before being slain.
The Æsir rejoice at Idun's recovery, eat her apples, regain strength and beauty, and vow to set Thiassi's eyes as a constellation in the heavens.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XX / BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII; lines 10017-10117
occurrences.motif_label: return of the long-absent husband
occurrences.basis: Euryclea repeatedly reports that Ulysses has come home, and Penelope descends to confront the man said to be her husband.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Euryclea wakes Penelope and announces that Ulysses has come home and killed the suitors who troubled his house.
Euryclea insists that Ulysses has returned, says he was the mistreated stranger, and says Telemachus kept his father's secret.
Penelope warns Euryclea not to exult, doubts that Ulysses has returned, and says perhaps a god ended the wicked suitors.
Penelope descends, considers whether to question or embrace Ulysses, sits opposite him by the fire, and fails to recognize him because of shabby clothing.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XX / BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII; lines 10017-10117
occurrences.motif_label: reclaiming the household through revenge
occurrences.basis: Ulysses' return is linked to killing the suitors, finding wife and son alive, and taking revenge in his own house.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Euryclea wakes Penelope and announces that Ulysses has come home and killed the suitors who troubled his house.
Euryclea describes hearing the suitors killed, seeing Ulysses bloodied among corpses, the bodies piled in the gatehouse, and a great purifying fire with sulphur.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XX / BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII; lines 10119-10211
occurrences.motif_label: returning husband recognized after long absence
occurrences.basis: The passage repeatedly frames Ulysses as the husband and father who has returned after twenty years and must be accepted by Penelope.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Telemachus asks why Penelope keeps away from his father after twenty years of absence and hardship, and says her heart is hard as stone.
Penelope says she is lost in astonishment and that if the man is truly Ulysses, they will understand one another through tokens known only to the two of them.
Ulysses smiles, accepts Penelope's proof, says she rejects him because of his dirt and bad clothes, and warns that they have killed the leading young men of Ithaca.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XX / BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII; lines 10119-10211
occurrences.motif_label: restoration of the hero's appearance
occurrences.basis: After Ulysses is washed, clothed, and beautified by Minerva, he appears stronger and more splendid in his own house before facing Penelope.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Eurynome washes, anoints, and clothes Ulysses; Minerva enhances his stature, strength, hair, and beauty; he sits opposite Penelope and calls her heart hard as iron.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XX / BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII; lines 10213-10296
occurrences.motif_label: recognition of the returned husband by a private sign
occurrences.basis: Penelope accepts Ulysses after he demonstrates unique knowledge of their bed, ending her fear of deception.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Penelope breaks down, embraces Ulysses, explains her fear of deception, invokes Helen, and says she can no longer mistrust him because he knows the secret of their bed.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XX / BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII; lines 10213-10296
occurrences.motif_label: reunion of long-separated spouses at the marriage bed
occurrences.basis: The couple weeps, embraces, is led to the prepared bed, and joyfully resumes their old bed after Ulysses’s return.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses weeps while clasping Penelope; the narration compares her welcome of him to swimmers reaching land after Neptune has wrecked their ship.

Eurynome and the nurse prepare the bed with torches and coverlets; Eurynome leads Ulysses and Penelope to their room by torchlight; the couple comes joyfully to their old bed while others stop dancing and sleep.
After love, Penelope tells of the suitors’ abuses in the house, and Ulysses tells all of his sufferings and the trouble he caused others while she listens until he finishes.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XX / BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII; lines 10213-10296
occurrences.motif_label: prophetic post-return journey to appease the sea god
occurrences.basis: Teiresias directs Ulysses, after return, to carry an oar inland, plant it, sacrifice to Neptune, return home, and honor the gods.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses tells Penelope that their troubles are not over and that Teiresias prophesied a long, difficult task when Ulysses went down into Hades to ask about his return.

Ulysses reports that Teiresias ordered him to travel with an oar to a country whose people have never heard of the sea, ships, salt, or oars, and where a wayfarer will ask if the oar is a winnowing shovel.

The prophecy instructs Ulysses to fix the oar in the ground, sacrifice a ram, bull, and boar to Neptune, return home, offer hecatombs to all the gods, and later die gently from the sea in old age while blessed by his people.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XX / BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII; lines 10213-10296
occurrences.motif_label: descent to the dead for knowledge of return
occurrences.basis: Ulysses says Teiresias prophesied concerning him on the day he went down into Hades to ask about his return and that of his companions.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses tells Penelope that their troubles are not over and that Teiresias prophesied a long, difficult task when Ulysses went down into Hades to ask about his return.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XX / BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII; lines 10298-10348
occurrences.motif_label: return after long wandering
occurrences.basis: Ulysses recounts the long journey that prevented his homecoming and tells Penelope they have at last come together.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses begins with victory over the Cicons, the land of the Lotus-eaters, the Cyclops, Aeolus, and the Laestrygonian destruction of all ships except his own.

Ulysses tells Penelope they have both endured troubles and are now together; he discusses restoring livestock, visiting his father, and tells her to remain upstairs with her women when news of the suitors' killing spreads.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XX / BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII; lines 10298-10348
occurrences.motif_label: hospitable conveyance home with gifts
occurrences.basis: The Phaeacians treat Ulysses as though divine, send him home by ship, and give him gold, bronze, and clothing.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The Phaeacians treat Ulysses as though he were a god, send him to his country by ship with gifts, and then deep sleep overtakes him and eases his sorrows.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII / BOOK XXIV; lines 10351-10444
occurrences.motif_label: Contrasted heroic deaths: honoured battlefield death and dishonoured homecoming death
occurrences.basis: Achilles is described as receiving fame through death at Troy, while Agamemnon laments destruction on his return by Aegisthus and his wife.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Agamemnon joins the heroic ghosts with those who died with him in Aegisthus’ house; Achilles says Agamemnon would have had a better end had he fallen at Troy.

The Argives build a noble tomb over the Hellespont; Thetis offers divine prizes for contests, and Agamemnon says Achilles’ fame and name endure, while his own return ended in destruction by Aegisthus and his wife.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII / BOOK XXIV; lines 10446-10532
occurrences.motif_label: disguised return of the absent husband
occurrences.basis: Ulysses returns after long absence disguised in rags as a beggar and is not recognized in his own house.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Telemachus comes first to town, then Ulysses comes with the swineherd, dressed in rags and leaning on a staff like a poor old beggar; none of the suitors recognizes him.
The suitors revile and throw things at Ulysses, but he endures being struck and insulted in his own house without speaking.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII / BOOK XXIV; lines 10446-10532
occurrences.motif_label: recognition test after long absence
occurrences.basis: Ulysses intends to see whether Laertes will recognize him after a long absence.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses and the others leave town and reach Laertes' well-tilled farm; Ulysses sends companions to prepare a pig for dinner while he tests whether his father will recognize him after long absence.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII / BOOK XXIV; lines 10534-10622
occurrences.motif_label: returning hero tests recognition before revealing himself
occurrences.basis: Ulysses returns to his father after twenty years but first uses a crafty assumed identity to test him, then reveals himself.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses removes his armour, gives it to Eumaeus and Philoetius, and turns into the vineyard to make trial of his father.
Ulysses sees Laertes worn, old, and sorrowful, weeps under a tall pear tree, considers immediate recognition, then decides to question him craftily.
Ulysses claims falsely that he is Eperitus from Alybas, son of king Apheidas, and that heaven drove him off course from Sicania to Ithaca.
Ulysses is moved, embraces and kisses Laertes, reveals himself as the son who has returned after twenty years, and says he has killed the suitors to punish their crimes.
Laertes replies that if the man truly is his son Ulysses, he must give manifest proof of identity.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII / BOOK XXIV; lines 10534-10622
occurrences.motif_label: identity requires proof after return
occurrences.basis: After Ulysses reveals himself as the returned son, Laertes requests manifest proof of his identity.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses is moved, embraces and kisses Laertes, reveals himself as the son who has returned after twenty years, and says he has killed the suitors to punish their crimes.
Laertes replies that if the man truly is his son Ulysses, he must give manifest proof of identity.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII / BOOK XXIV; lines 10624-10722
occurrences.motif_label: Return proven by bodily mark and remembered gifts
occurrences.basis: Ulysses’ return is recognized through the scar and detailed recollection of trees and vines given by Laertes.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses proves his identity by showing a scar from a boar’s tusk received on Mt. Parnassus and by naming the pear, apple, fig trees and rows of vines Laertes had given or promised him.
Laertes is overcome by the proofs, embraces Ulysses, says the gods are still in Olympus if the suitors have been punished, and fears retaliation by Ithaca and the Cephallenians.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII / BOOK XXIV; lines 10624-10722
occurrences.motif_label: Restored household and loyal recognition
occurrences.basis: Dolius and his sons greet Ulysses as restored by heaven, and household members gather around him in due order.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Dolius and his sons arrive for the meal, recognize Ulysses, greet and embrace him; Dolius kisses Ulysses’ hand and says heaven has restored him home.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII / BOOK XXIV; lines 10724-10815
occurrences.motif_label: returning ruler’s legitimacy confirmed after vengeance
occurrences.basis: Jove states that Ulysses has returned, taken revenge, and should continue to rule under the settlement.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Jove says Ulysses has taken revenge and proposes that the parties swear a solemn covenant, Ulysses continue to rule, the others forget the massacre, and peace and plenty reign.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII / BOOK XXIV / FOOTNOTES:; lines 11174-11276
occurrences.motif_label: return to homeland under sleep
occurrences.basis: The note links Ulysses' sleep with the harbor used for his landing in Ithaca.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The note says Ulysses' sleep is being prepared and is important because the harbor used for his landing in Ithaca was about two miles from where he is speaking with Alcinous.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII / BOOK XXIV / FOOTNOTES:; lines 11278-11377
occurrences.motif_label: hero's return from wandering voyage
occurrences.basis: The notes mention Ulysses's voyage, his return from an unfortunate voyage, and the larger context of his wanderings.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The note says 'floating' should not be taken literally of Aeolus's island; Ulysses stayed there for a month and found it in the same place when he returned.
The notes state that during the first year of Ulysses's wanderings Telemachus would have been only eleven or twelve.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII / BOOK XXIV / FOOTNOTES:; lines 11278-11377
occurrences.motif_label: prophecy of loss before homecoming
occurrences.basis: The note reports a prophecy ending with the loss of all comrades and discusses an added allusion to suitors.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The note says a corresponding prophecy ends with the loss of all comrades and that an expanded passage adds allusion to the suitors.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: The Odyssey / PREFACE TO FIRST EDITION; lines 113-185
occurrences.motif_label: wandering hero seeking return
occurrences.basis: The quoted opening centers on the man who wanders widely, suffers on the deep, and strives for his own life and the return of his company.

evidence.quote_or_summary: “Tell me, Muse, of that man ... who wandered far and wide” after Troy and suffered on the deep while seeking life and return.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: The Odyssey / PREFACE TO FIRST EDITION; lines 113-185
occurrences.motif_label: circular island voyage returning to point of origin
occurrences.basis: The preface describes Ulysses' voyages near Sicily as a periplus from Trapani back to Trapani via named islands and straits.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The preface states that the Odyssey was written at and drawn from Trapani, and that Ulysses' nearby voyages form a periplus from Trapani back to Trapani via the Lipari islands, the Straits of Messina, and Pantellaria.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XXII / BOOK XXIII / BOOK XXIV / FOOTNOTES:; lines 11379-11488
occurrences.motif_label: return under concealment by night, sleep, and fog
occurrences.basis: The note says Ulysses leaves after dark, falls into deep sleep, and wakes on a foggy morning before recognizing the situation.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The note explains that Ulysses is made to set out after dark, fall into deep sleep, and wake on a foggy morning so the audience can accept the setting.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK I / BOOK II / BOOK III / TELEMACHUS VISITS NESTOR AT PYLOS.; lines 1232-1327
occurrences.motif_label: difficult homecoming after war
occurrences.basis: Nestor describes the Achaean return from Troy as divided, delayed, and dangerous, with uncertainty over who reached home safely.

evidence.quote_or_summary: After Priam's city was sacked, Jove vexed the Argives on their voyage home, and Minerva's displeasure brought about a quarrel between the sons of Atreus.
Jove is said to hatch mischief; some Achaeans launch ships, others remain with Agamemnon, and later some turn back under Ulysses while Nestor presses onward.
At Lesbos, Nestor's group debates the route, asks heaven for a sign, and is shown that crossing the open sea to Euboea will get them soonest out of danger.
Nestor reports safe returns for some leaders, says Agamemnon died at Aegisthus' hands, and says Orestes killed false Aegisthus, the murderer of his father.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK I / BOOK II / BOOK III / TELEMACHUS VISITS NESTOR AT PYLOS.; lines 1329-1422
occurrences.motif_label: imperiled return and unsafe homecoming
occurrences.basis: Minerva contrasts arduous safe return with Agamemnon's quick return and murder at home; Nestor's narrative includes Menelaus' storm-delayed return and warns Telemachus about dangers at home during absence.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Minerva says heaven can save a man, that safe homecoming is worth suffering for, and that not even the gods can save a man when his hour of death comes.
Near the Malean heads Jove sends hard winds and high waves; Menelaus' fleet is divided, some ships are wrecked near Crete, and five ships are carried to Egypt.
Nestor warns Telemachus not to stay away too long or leave property among dangerous people, and advises him to visit Menelaus, who will speak truthfully.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK I / BOOK II / BOOK III / TELEMACHUS VISITS NESTOR AT PYLOS.; lines 1329-1422
occurrences.motif_label: filial return to avenge a murdered father
occurrences.basis: Orestes returns from Athens and kills Aegisthus, explicitly identified as the murderer of his father.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Aegisthus rules Mycene seven years after killing Agamemnon; in the eighth year Orestes returns from Athens, kills him, and holds funeral rites and a banquet.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK II / BOOK III / TELEMACHUS VISITS NESTOR AT PYLOS. / BOOK IV; lines 1561-1661
occurrences.motif_label: difficult return from war through many lands
occurrences.basis: Menelaus says he travelled widely and suffered hardship for nearly eight years before reaching home with his fleet.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Menelaus says no one can equal Jove's immortal house, then says he traveled much and suffered hardship for nearly eight years before returning with his fleet through Cyprus, Phoenicia, Egypt, Ethiopia, Sidon, the Erembians, and Libya.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK II / BOOK III / TELEMACHUS VISITS NESTOR AT PYLOS. / BOOK IV; lines 1762-1847
occurrences.motif_label: Threatened household and expected avenging return
occurrences.basis: Telemachus reports suitors consuming his estate and courting his mother; Menelaus says Ulysses would destroy them if he returned.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Telemachus says he came to learn about his father, describes suitors wasting his estate while courting his mother, and asks Menelaus as a suppliant to tell plainly what he saw or heard about Ulysses.

Menelaus is shocked, says the suitors would usurp a brave man's bed, compares them to a hind's young in a lion's lair, says Ulysses would swiftly punish them if he returned, and promises to report what the old man of the sea told him.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK II / BOOK III / TELEMACHUS VISITS NESTOR AT PYLOS. / BOOK IV; lines 1849-1948
occurrences.motif_label: Obstructed homeward voyage requiring divine disclosure
occurrences.basis: The speaker is detained and seeks instruction on how to sail home, with Proteus identified as the one who can tell him the route.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The speaker says the gods detained him in Egypt because his hecatombs had not given them full satisfaction and the gods are strict about their dues.
The speaker asks which immortal is hindering him and how to reach home; Idothea says Proteus lives under the sea, serves Neptune, knows the sea bottom, and can reveal the voyage and home news.

Idothea instructs the speaker to seize Proteus after he counts the seals and sleeps, hold him through transformations into creatures, fire, and water, and question him when he returns to his original form.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: The Odyssey / PREFACE TO FIRST EDITION; lines 187-272
occurrences.motif_label: delayed return home
occurrences.basis: Odysseus is fated to return to Ithaca but is delayed by Calypso and Poseidon's hostility while longing for home.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Odysseus alone is away from home, craving wife and return, while Calypso holds him in hollow caves and wants him for her lord.
The gods ordain Odysseus' return to Ithaca, yet he remains subject to labours and Poseidon's continual rage until he reaches his country.

Athene pities Odysseus, who suffers on a sea-girt wooded island, the navel of the sea, where a goddess, daughter of Atlas, holds him and woos him to forget Ithaca; Odysseus longs for the smoke of his land and desires death.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK II / BOOK III / TELEMACHUS VISITS NESTOR AT PYLOS. / BOOK IV; lines 1950-2039
occurrences.motif_label: sacrifice required before successful return
occurrences.basis: Menelaus cannot finish his voyage until he returns to Egypt and offers holy hecatombs to the gods.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Proteus says Menelaus must sacrifice to Jove and the gods, return to Egypt, and offer holy hecatombs before the gods will let him finish his voyage.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK II / BOOK III / TELEMACHUS VISITS NESTOR AT PYLOS. / BOOK IV; lines 1950-2039
occurrences.motif_label: divine obstruction and release of homecoming
occurrences.basis: Menelaus asks which immortal hinders him, and Proteus says the gods will permit the voyage after sacrifice.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Menelaus asks the old man which immortal is hindering him and how he may sail the sea to reach home.
Proteus says Menelaus must sacrifice to Jove and the gods, return to Egypt, and offer holy hecatombs before the gods will let him finish his voyage.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK II / BOOK III / TELEMACHUS VISITS NESTOR AT PYLOS. / BOOK IV; lines 1950-2039
occurrences.motif_label: homecoming hero murdered by treacherous feast
occurrences.basis: Agamemnon returns home but Aegisthus plots an ambush, invites him to a banquet, and kills him after the feast.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Agamemnon and his ships escape under Juno's protection, are driven by a gale, then reach home, where Agamemnon kisses his native soil and weeps for joy.
Aegisthus has a paid watchman look for Agamemnon, sets warriors in ambush, prepares a banquet, invites Agamemnon, and kills him after the feast along with the followers present.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK II / BOOK III / TELEMACHUS VISITS NESTOR AT PYLOS. / BOOK IV; lines 1950-2039
occurrences.motif_label: detained wanderer unable to return
occurrences.basis: Ulysses is alive on Calypso's island but cannot get home because he has no ships or sailors.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Proteus says the third man is Ulysses of Ithaca, alive on an island, sorrowing in Calypso's house, kept prisoner and unable to return for lack of ships and sailors.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK II / BOOK III / TELEMACHUS VISITS NESTOR AT PYLOS. / BOOK IV; lines 2041-2133
occurrences.motif_label: ambush during return voyage
occurrences.basis: Antinous proposes lying in wait for Telemachus in the straits between Ithaca and Samos when Telemachus returns from his voyage.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Antinous is angry, says Telemachus has escaped with a picked crew, asks for a ship and twenty men, and proposes lying in wait in the straits between Ithaca and Samos so Telemachus will rue his search for news of his father; the others approve.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK II / BOOK III / TELEMACHUS VISITS NESTOR AT PYLOS. / BOOK IV; lines 2135-2239
occurrences.motif_label: threatened heir ambushed on return
occurrences.basis: Telemachus, son of Ulysses and heir to the house, is targeted for murder as he comes home, and Penelope frames the danger as an attempt to exterminate the family line.

evidence.quote_or_summary: “They are going to try and murder Telemachus as he is coming home from Pylos and Lacedaemon” after seeking news of his father.

Penelope collapses in grief, the maids weep around her, and she laments losing Ulysses and now having her son at the mercy of winds and waves; she orders Dolius to inform Laertes of the threat to their race.
Penelope lies upstairs unable to eat or drink, wonders whether Telemachus will escape, is compared to a trapped lioness surrounded by huntsmen, and falls asleep.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK II / BOOK III / TELEMACHUS VISITS NESTOR AT PYLOS. / BOOK IV; lines 2241-2286
occurrences.motif_label: return endangered by ambush
occurrences.basis: Telemachus is expected to come back, but the suitors plan to kill him before he can return and lie in ambush at Asteris.

evidence.quote_or_summary: “Your son has done them no wrong, so he will yet come back to you.”
Penelope addresses the figure as her sister, laments her lost brave husband, fears for her son who has gone by ship, and says enemies are plotting to kill him before he returns home.
The suitors sail over the sea intent on murdering Telemachus and place themselves in ambush.
Asteris is described as a small rocky islet in mid-channel between Ithaca and Samos, with a harbor on either side where a ship can lie.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK III / TELEMACHUS VISITS NESTOR AT PYLOS. / BOOK IV / BOOK V; lines 2289-2384
occurrences.motif_label: decreed return of the detained hero
occurrences.basis: The passage centers on a divine decision that Ulysses, detained by Calypso and grieving far from home, must be released and return to his country, house, and friends.

evidence.quote_or_summary: At the divine council, Minerva pities Ulysses in Calypso’s house, says Calypso will not release him, and reports danger to Telemachus from would-be murderers.
Jove orders Mercury to tell Calypso that Ulysses is decreed to return: he will travel by raft for twenty perilous days to Scheria, and the Phaeacians will send him home with gifts.
Ulysses is not in the cave but is on the sea-shore as usual, looking over the ocean with tears and sorrow.
“Jove says that you are to let this man go at once ... but shall return to his house and country and see his friends again.”

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK III / TELEMACHUS VISITS NESTOR AT PYLOS. / BOOK IV / BOOK V; lines 2289-2384
occurrences.motif_label: perilous sea voyage toward home
occurrences.basis: Jove states that Ulysses will travel without divine or human convoy, endure twenty days on a raft, and reach Scheria before being sent home.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Jove orders Mercury to tell Calypso that Ulysses is decreed to return: he will travel by raft for twenty perilous days to Scheria, and the Phaeacians will send him home with gifts.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK III / TELEMACHUS VISITS NESTOR AT PYLOS. / BOOK IV / BOOK V; lines 2386-2472
occurrences.motif_label: release and departure of the detained hero
occurrences.basis: Mercury orders Calypso to send Ulysses away, and Calypso offers means for him to voyage home.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Mercury says to send Ulysses away or Jove will be angry and punish Calypso.
Calypso tells Ulysses she will send him away, instructs him to cut beams and build a large raft with an upper deck, and promises bread, wine, water, clothes, and a fair wind if the gods allow.
Ulysses says Penelope is mortal and less beautiful than Calypso, but he wants to get home and will endure further wreck or suffering as part of his troubles.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK III / TELEMACHUS VISITS NESTOR AT PYLOS. / BOOK IV / BOOK V; lines 2386-2472
occurrences.motif_label: mortal chooses home and wife over immortality with a goddess
occurrences.basis: Calypso offers immortality if Ulysses stays; Ulysses acknowledges her superiority to Penelope in beauty but says he wants only to get home.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Calypso asks whether Ulysses would leave at once and says that if he knew his future suffering he would stay, keep house with her, and let her make him immortal despite his longing for his wife.
Ulysses says Penelope is mortal and less beautiful than Calypso, but he wants to get home and will endure further wreck or suffering as part of his troubles.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK III / TELEMACHUS VISITS NESTOR AT PYLOS. / BOOK IV / BOOK V; lines 2474-2559
occurrences.motif_label: homeward return by sea
occurrences.basis: Ulysses sails by raft, keeps the Bear to his left as instructed, approaches the Phaeacian coast, and speaks of trouble before getting back home.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses steers by the Pleiads, Bootes, and the Bear, following Calypso’s instruction, and after eighteen days sees the mountains of the Phaeacian coast.
Neptune gathers clouds, grasps his trident, stirs the sea, and rouses all winds; Ulysses laments the blackened sky, the sea, and the likelihood of a pitiable death at sea.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK III / TELEMACHUS VISITS NESTOR AT PYLOS. / BOOK IV / BOOK V; lines 2561-2653
occurrences.motif_label: perilous water passage toward safe land
occurrences.basis: Ulysses leaves the wrecked raft, swims for the Phaeacian coast, endures two nights and days in the sea, sees land, and seeks a landing place.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Neptune sends a great wave that breaks the raft; Ulysses rides a plank, removes Calypso's clothes, binds Ino's veil under his arms, plunges into the sea to swim, and Neptune taunts him before driving to Aegae.
Minerva helps Ulysses by stilling the winds except for a north breeze meant to calm the waters until he reaches the Phaeacian land safely.
Ulysses floats for two nights and two days with death near; on the third day the wind falls, he sees nearby land and trees, and swims strongly toward dry ground.
The coast is loud with surf, rocks, spray, and no harbor; Ulysses fears being smashed on the rocks, driven back to sea, or attacked by a sea monster bred by Amphitrite because Neptune is angry.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK IV / BOOK V / BOOK VI / THE MEETING BETWEEN NAUSICAA AND ULYSSES.; lines 2694-2792
occurrences.motif_label: divine intervention to enable a hero's return
occurrences.basis: Minerva explicitly goes to Alcinous' house in furtherance of Ulysses' return while Ulysses sleeps from toil.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses sleeps; Minerva goes to the Phaeacians. The Phaeacians had moved from Hypereia near the Cyclopes to Scheria under Nausithous, who built and divided the city; Alcinous now reigns, and Minerva goes to his house to further Ulysses' return.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: The Odyssey / PREFACE TO FIRST EDITION; lines 274-318
occurrences.motif_label: Return of Ulysses
occurrences.basis: The passage explicitly identifies one component poem as The Return of Ulysses.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The first poem is called The Return of Ulysses; the Muse is asked to sing it, and it includes the Phaeacian episode and Ulysses’ account of adventures in Books ix-xii.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK IV / BOOK V / BOOK VI / THE MEETING BETWEEN NAUSICAA AND ULYSSES.; lines 2882-2972
occurrences.motif_label: Homecoming secured through supplication
occurrences.basis: Nausicaa says Ulysses may hope to see his own country again if he gains her mother over by clasping her knees.

evidence.locator: lines 2970-2972 and following passage text in supplied range
evidence.quote_or_summary: Nausicaa instructs Ulysses to ask for Alcinous's house, pass through gates and courts, approach her mother by the fire as she spins purple wool, clasp her knees, and gain hope of returning home.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK IV / BOOK V / BOOK VI / THE MEETING BETWEEN NAUSICAA AND ULYSSES.; lines 2974-2989
occurrences.motif_label: homecoming obstructed by an angry deity
occurrences.basis: Neptune is described as still furious and trying to prevent Ulysses from getting home.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Minerva hears the prayer but does not appear openly because she fears Neptune, who remains furious and tries to prevent Ulysses from getting home.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK VI / THE MEETING BETWEEN NAUSICAA AND ULYSSES. / BOOK VII / RECEPTION OF ULYSSES AT THE PALACE OF KING ALCINOUS.; lines 2992-3088
occurrences.motif_label: homecoming dependent on gaining a queen's goodwill
occurrences.basis: Minerva tells Ulysses that if he gains Arete's goodwill he may hope to see his friends and return safely to his home and country.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Minerva points out the house, tells Ulysses to seek Arete, recounts the descent of Alcinous and Arete from Neptune, describes Arete's exceptional honor, and says her goodwill may enable Ulysses' return home.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK VI / THE MEETING BETWEEN NAUSICAA AND ULYSSES. / BOOK VII / RECEPTION OF ULYSSES AT THE PALACE OF KING ALCINOUS.; lines 3090-3174
occurrences.motif_label: safe escort for homeward return
occurrences.basis: Alcinous proposes a banquet and discussion of how to send the guest back rejoicing to his own country without trouble or harm.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Alcinous tells the Phaeacian councillors to go to bed, announces a sacrificial banquet for the guest, and says they will discuss escorting him safely and joyfully to his own country.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK VI / THE MEETING BETWEEN NAUSICAA AND ULYSSES. / BOOK VII / RECEPTION OF ULYSSES AT THE PALACE OF KING ALCINOUS.; lines 3176-3259
occurrences.motif_label: homeward return after suffering
occurrences.basis: Ulysses explicitly asks for help getting home and frames his wish around seeing his property, bondsmen, and house again.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses asks to sup despite sorrow and asks that at daybreak they help him get home.
Everyone approves arranging an escort; drink offerings are made, and the others go home.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK VI / THE MEETING BETWEEN NAUSICAA AND ULYSSES. / BOOK VII / RECEPTION OF ULYSSES AT THE PALACE OF KING ALCINOUS.; lines 3261-3292
occurrences.motif_label: promised return home by escorted voyage
occurrences.basis: Alcinous promises to arrange an escort by ship to Ulysses' home or wherever he chooses, and Ulysses prays that this will let him return to his country.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Alcinous says no one shall keep Ulysses there against his will and promises to address the matter of his escort the next day.
Alcinous says Ulysses can sleep during the voyage while men sail him over smooth waters to his own home or wherever he wishes.
Ulysses is glad and prays to Father Jove that Alcinous may do as promised, gaining an imperishable name while Ulysses returns to his country.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: THE MEETING BETWEEN NAUSICAA AND ULYSSES. / BOOK VII / RECEPTION OF ULYSSES AT THE PALACE OF KING ALCINOUS. / BOOK VIII; lines 3295-3396
occurrences.motif_label: divine helper in disguise aids the hero's return
occurrences.basis: Minerva disguises herself as a servant, summons the Phaeacians to hear the stranger, and enhances Ulysses' appearance in a context where he seeks escort home.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Minerva takes the form of one of Alcinous' servants, goes around town, and urges Phaeacian aldermen and councillors to attend the assembly and hear the long-voyaging stranger.
The citizens crowd the assembly; Minerva beautifies Ulysses around the head and shoulders and makes him look taller and stouter so he will impress the Phaeacians and do well in trials of skill.

Alcinous tells the Phaeacian leaders that the stranger wants an escort, orders a new ship and fifty-two young sailors prepared, and invites the leaders to help entertain the guest with Demodocus singing.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: THE MEETING BETWEEN NAUSICAA AND ULYSSES. / BOOK VII / RECEPTION OF ULYSSES AT THE PALACE OF KING ALCINOUS. / BOOK VIII; lines 3398-3494
occurrences.motif_label: Homeward return delayed by testing among hosts
occurrences.basis: Ulysses says he seeks aid for his return, while his hosts draw him into athletic competition before that return proceeds.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Laodamas describes the stranger as powerfully built but recently harmed by the sea, invites him to compete, and says the ship and crew for his return are ready.
“my mind is set rather on cares than contests”; Ulysses says he comes as a suppliant asking help for his return home.
Ulysses challenges the young men to compete in boxing, wrestling, running, or other sports, but excludes Laodamas because he is his guest and should not challenge the host’s family.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: THE MEETING BETWEEN NAUSICAA AND ULYSSES. / BOOK VII / RECEPTION OF ULYSSES AT THE PALACE OF KING ALCINOUS. / BOOK VIII; lines 3599-3696
occurrences.motif_label: hope for safe homecoming
occurrences.basis: Euryalus wishes Ulysses a safe return, and Ulysses tells Nausicaa he hopes Jove grants that he may reach home.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Euryalus promises satisfaction, gives Ulysses a bronze sword with silver hilt and ivory scabbard, apologizes, and wishes him a safe return.
Nausicaa asks Ulysses to remember her because she saved his life; Ulysses says he will bless her as his guardian angel if he reaches home.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: THE MEETING BETWEEN NAUSICAA AND ULYSSES. / BOOK VII / RECEPTION OF ULYSSES AT THE PALACE OF KING ALCINOUS. / BOOK VIII; lines 3698-3785
occurrences.motif_label: return home by extraordinary sea escort
occurrences.basis: Alcinous asks for the guest's homeland so that Phaeacian ships may take him there, and the ships are described as knowing destinations and safely crossing the sea.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Alcinous asks the guest to end concealment, state the name given by his parents, and identify his country, nation, and city so Phaeacian ships can take him there.
Alcinous says Phaeacian ships lack pilots and rudders, understand thoughts and desires, know all cities and countries, and cross the sea safely even in mist and cloud.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: THE MEETING BETWEEN NAUSICAA AND ULYSSES. / BOOK VII / RECEPTION OF ULYSSES AT THE PALACE OF KING ALCINOUS. / BOOK VIII; lines 3787-3798
occurrences.motif_label: return from Troy causing grief
occurrences.basis: The passage explicitly mentions the return of the Argive Danaans from Troy and the addressee’s unhappiness on hearing about it.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The speaker asks why the addressee is unhappy on hearing of “the return of the Argive Danaans from Troy.”

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK VII / RECEPTION OF ULYSSES AT THE PALACE OF KING ALCINOUS. / BOOK VIII / BOOK IX; lines 3801-3898
occurrences.motif_label: hazardous return voyage from war
occurrences.basis: Ulysses frames the following adventures as events met on his return from Troy, including hostile encounters, storms, and delay before reaching later lands.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Calypso kept Ulysses in her cave and wanted marriage; Circe also wanted marriage; Ulysses says home and parents are dearer than a splendid foreign home, and he will tell of adventures on his return from Troy by Jove's will.

After sailing from Troy to Ismarus, Ulysses' force sacks the city of the Cicons, takes wives and booty, but the men ignore his advice to leave and remain drinking wine and slaughtering livestock on the shore.
Jove raises the North wind into a hurricane; clouds hide land and sky, the wind tears the sails, and the crew rows toward land, remaining there two days and nights in distress.

After setting sail again, adverse wind and currents drive Ulysses off course near Cape Malea and Cythera; after nine days of foul winds, the fleet reaches the land of the Lotus-eaters and lands for water and food.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK VII / RECEPTION OF ULYSSES AT THE PALACE OF KING ALCINOUS. / BOOK VIII / BOOK IX; lines 3801-3898
occurrences.motif_label: home-longing resisting foreign divine marriage
occurrences.basis: Ulysses says Calypso and Circe wanted marriage, but he was not persuaded and emphasizes country and parents as dearer than a splendid foreign home.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Calypso kept Ulysses in her cave and wanted marriage; Circe also wanted marriage; Ulysses says home and parents are dearer than a splendid foreign home, and he will tell of adventures on his return from Troy by Jove's will.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK VII / RECEPTION OF ULYSSES AT THE PALACE OF KING ALCINOUS. / BOOK VIII / BOOK IX; lines 3801-3898
occurrences.motif_label: enchanted or dangerous food causing forgetfulness of home
occurrences.basis: Lotus makes its eaters stop caring about home or return, requiring Ulysses to force the affected men back to the ships.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses sends three men to learn about the people; the Lotus-eaters do not harm them but give them lotus, after which the eaters stop caring about home or reporting back and want to remain eating lotus.
Ulysses forces the lotus-eaters among his men back to the ships, ties them under the benches, and orders the rest aboard lest they taste lotus and stop wanting to go home.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: PREFACE TO SECOND EDITION / HENRY FESTING JONES. / THE ODYSSEY / BOOK I; lines 390-492
occurrences.motif_label: blocked homecoming and planned return
occurrences.basis: Ulysses longs for home, is detained and opposed, and the gods agree to help him return.

evidence.quote_or_summary: All surviving warriors have returned except Ulysses, who longs for his wife and country but is detained by Calypso in a large cave; the gods decide he should return, while Neptune still persecutes him.

Minerva says her heart bleeds for Ulysses on a lonely sea-girt forest island, where Atlas' daughter keeps him with blandishments so that he longs for home; she also recalls his burnt sacrifices to Jove.
Jove praises Ulysses but explains that Neptune is angry because Ulysses blinded Polyphemus, son of Neptune and Thoosa; Neptune prevents the return, but the gods can plan together to help Ulysses.

Minerva proposes sending Mercury to Ogygia to announce the decision to Calypso, while she goes to Ithaca to strengthen Telemachus, confront the suitors, and send him to Sparta and Pylos for news of Ulysses.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK VII / RECEPTION OF ULYSSES AT THE PALACE OF KING ALCINOUS. / BOOK VIII / BOOK IX; lines 4170-4268
occurrences.motif_label: Cursed or obstructed homecoming
occurrences.basis: Polyphemus prays that Ulysses may never reach home, or may arrive late, suffering, without his men, in another man's ship, and find trouble in his house.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Polyphemus raises his hands to heaven and prays to Neptune that Ulysses may never reach home alive, or may return late, in distress, after losing all his men, in another man's ship, and find trouble at home.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK VII / RECEPTION OF ULYSSES AT THE PALACE OF KING ALCINOUS. / BOOK VIII / BOOK IX; lines 4270-4293
occurrences.motif_label: return to companions after escape from death
occurrences.basis: Ulysses' party reaches the island where comrades have been anxiously awaiting them and later sails onward, glad to have escaped death.

evidence.quote_or_summary: At the island where the rest of the ships were left, the returning men find comrades lamenting and waiting, beach the vessel, land the Cyclops' sheep, and divide them equitably.
The men feast through the day, camp on the beach at night, and at Dawn board, row over the grey sea, and sail on sorrowful but glad to have escaped death despite lost comrades.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK VIII / BOOK IX / BOOK X / AEOLUS, THE LAESTRYGONES, CIRCE.; lines 4296-4397
occurrences.motif_label: sealed object opened by mistrustful companions causes loss of homecoming
occurrences.basis: The fleet nearly reaches home, but companions suspect treasure in the sealed sack, open it, and release a storm that carries them away from their country.

evidence.quote_or_summary: After nine days and nights, native land appears on the horizon close enough for stubble fires to be seen; Ulysses, exhausted from steering, falls asleep.
The men talk among themselves, suspecting Ulysses is bringing home gold and silver in Aeolus's sack, and urge one another to inspect it.
The men loose the sack; the winds howl out, raise a storm, and drive the lamenting fleet away from its own country back toward the Aeolian island.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK VIII / BOOK IX / BOOK X / AEOLUS, THE LAESTRYGONES, CIRCE.; lines 4680-4781
occurrences.motif_label: hero's journey to the underworld before return
occurrences.basis: Ulysses seeks homeward passage, but Circe says he must first go to the house of Hades and Proserpine.

evidence.quote_or_summary: After feasting, Ulysses gets into bed with Circe and asks her to keep her promise about furthering his homeward voyage.
Circe says they need not stay, but must first go to the house of Hades and Proserpine to consult the ghost of Teiresias, who retains understanding in death.
