Ulysses tells the men they think they are going home, but Circe has explained they must go to Hades and Proserpine to consult Teiresias.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK X / AEOLUS, THE LAESTRYGONES, CIRCE. / BOOK XI / THE VISIT TO THE DEAD.88; lines 4876-4967
occurrences.motif_label: prophetic conditions for return home
occurrences.basis: Teiresias gives Odysseus conditional instructions and forecasts the hardships, losses, revenge, and later rites connected to his return.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Teiresias says heaven will make Odysseus' return hard and that Neptune still bears a bitter grudge because Odysseus blinded his son.
At Thrinacia Odysseus will find the Sun's sheep and cattle; if the flocks are left unharmed, he may reach Ithaca after hardship, but if they are harmed his ship and men will be destroyed.
Odysseus may return after losing his men and will find his house overrun by people devouring his substance while courting his wife; he will take revenge on the suitors by force or fraud.

Odysseus must carry a well-made oar to a country where people do not know the sea, ships, or oars; when a wayfarer calls it a winnowing shovel, he must plant it and sacrifice a ram, bull, and boar to Neptune.
After the inland sacrifice, Odysseus must return home, offer hecatombs to all the gods, and will eventually die gently from the sea in old age and peace.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK X / AEOLUS, THE LAESTRYGONES, CIRCE. / BOOK XI / THE VISIT TO THE DEAD.88; lines 4876-4967
occurrences.motif_label: journey to a land ignorant of the sea
occurrences.basis: Odysseus must carry an oar inland until people no longer recognize it as an oar, then plant it and perform sacrifice.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Odysseus must carry a well-made oar to a country where people do not know the sea, ships, or oars; when a wayfarer calls it a winnowing shovel, he must plant it and sacrifice a ram, bull, and boar to Neptune.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: PREFACE TO SECOND EDITION / HENRY FESTING JONES. / THE ODYSSEY / BOOK I; lines 494-587
occurrences.motif_label: absent father’s expected return
occurrences.basis: Telemachus laments Ulysses’ absence and imagines the suitors’ fear if he came back; Minerva says Ulysses is not dead and will find a way home.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Telemachus says the suitors’ entertainment is paid for from his absent father’s goods, imagines their fear if Ulysses returned, says he does not expect to see him again, and asks the visitor’s identity, origin, ship, people, and prior connection to the house.

Minerva answers as Mentes, son of Anchialus and king of the Taphians, describes a trading voyage and ship at Rheithron under wooded Neritum, claims old family friendship, describes Laertes’ isolation, and says Ulysses is not dead and will find a way home.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK X / AEOLUS, THE LAESTRYGONES, CIRCE. / BOOK XI / THE VISIT TO THE DEAD.88; lines 5070-5169
occurrences.motif_label: generous host gift and escort for a returning guest
occurrences.basis: The Phaeacian hosts discuss gifts, delay, and escort for Ulysses' homeward return.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The queen asks the Phaeacians whether Ulysses is tall, good-looking, and clever, and urges them not to send him away hastily or be stingy with gifts.
Alcinous says Ulysses should stay until tomorrow while gifts are gathered and that escorting him concerns all the Phaeacians, especially himself.
Ulysses says he would gladly stay even twelve months if then sent home with noble gifts, returning to Ithaca fuller-handed and more respected.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK X / AEOLUS, THE LAESTRYGONES, CIRCE. / BOOK XI / THE VISIT TO THE DEAD.88; lines 5070-5169
occurrences.motif_label: returning king murdered at a feast
occurrences.basis: Agamemnon says he was invited to Aegisthus' house, feasted, and then killed with his companions amid banquet objects.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Agamemnon denies death by Neptune's storm and says Aegisthus and his wife killed him after feasting him; his comrades were slain around the mixing bowl and loaded tables, with the ground reeking with blood.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK X / AEOLUS, THE LAESTRYGONES, CIRCE. / BOOK XI / THE VISIT TO THE DEAD.88; lines 5070-5169
occurrences.motif_label: treacherous spouse versus faithful spouse at homecoming
occurrences.basis: Agamemnon condemns Clytemnestra for murdering him and contrasts her with Penelope, whom he calls admirable and unlikely to murder Ulysses.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Agamemnon says Cassandra screamed as Clytemnestra killed her; he lay dying with a sword in his body, and Clytemnestra did not close his lips or eyes.
Agamemnon advises Ulysses not to tell even his wife everything, but says Penelope is admirable and unlikely to murder him; he expects Ulysses and his grown son to have a joyful meeting.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK X / AEOLUS, THE LAESTRYGONES, CIRCE. / BOOK XI / THE VISIT TO THE DEAD.88; lines 5070-5169
occurrences.motif_label: secret return after warning of betrayal
occurrences.basis: Agamemnon advises Ulysses to conceal knowledge even from his wife and to bring his ship to Ithaca secretly.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Agamemnon advises Ulysses not to tell even his wife everything, but says Penelope is admirable and unlikely to murder him; he expects Ulysses and his grown son to have a joyful meeting.
Agamemnon advises Ulysses to bring his ship to Ithaca secretly and asks whether Ulysses has news of his son Orestes.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK X / AEOLUS, THE LAESTRYGONES, CIRCE. / BOOK XI / THE VISIT TO THE DEAD.88; lines 5271-5317
occurrences.motif_label: return from the realm of the dead
occurrences.basis: Ulysses leaves the gathering ghosts, returns to his ship, and departs down the river Oceanus.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Thousands of ghosts gather with appalling cries, and Ulysses fears Proserpine may send up the Gorgon's head from Hades.
Ulysses hastens back to his ship, orders his men aboard, and the ship goes down the stream of Oceanus, first rowing and then with a fair wind.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XI / THE VISIT TO THE DEAD.88 / BOOK XII / THE SIRENS, SCYLLA AND CHARYBDIS, THE CATTLE OF THE SUN.; lines 5320-5420
occurrences.motif_label: Living descent to the house of the dead and return
occurrences.basis: Circe explicitly says the group went down alive to Hades and returned, and the passage opens after their departure from Oceanus toward Aeaea.

evidence.quote_or_summary: After clearing Oceanus, the voyagers reach Aeaea, draw the ship onto the sands, sleep on shore, and wait for dawn.

Circe, knowing they returned from Hades, arrives with servants bringing bread, meat, and wine; she calls their living descent to Hades bold, says they will have died twice, and promises to explain the route.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XI / THE VISIT TO THE DEAD.88 / BOOK XII / THE SIRENS, SCYLLA AND CHARYBDIS, THE CATTLE OF THE SUN.; lines 5422-5511
occurrences.motif_label: Return endangered by successive sea trials
occurrences.basis: Circe says Ulysses may reach Ithaca after hardship if the herds are unharmed, and the passage immediately continues with sequential maritime dangers.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The goddess warns that if the flocks are left unharmed Ulysses may reach Ithaca after hardship, but if harmed, the ship and comrades will be destroyed and Ulysses will return late and in bad condition if he survives.
After dawn, the goddess returns inland; Ulysses boards, the crew looses the ship and rows, and Circe sends a favorable following wind that fills the sails.
After the island, Ulysses sees a great wave with rising spray and hears loud roaring; the frightened men release their oars, and the ship stops.
Ulysses exhorts the crew, recalling their escape from the Cyclops's cave, tells them to trust Jove and row hard, and orders the coxswain to steer away from steaming rapids and hug the rock.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XI / THE VISIT TO THE DEAD.88 / BOOK XII / THE SIRENS, SCYLLA AND CHARYBDIS, THE CATTLE OF THE SUN.; lines 5610-5710
occurrences.motif_label: Sole survivor on wreckage after divine storm
occurrences.basis: The crew is destroyed at sea, while Ulysses survives by lashing together mast and keel and continuing his journey on the wreckage.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Jove releases thunderbolts; the ship is struck, filled with fire and brimstone, and the men fall into the sea and are deprived of homecoming.
Ulysses remains with the wreck until the sides separate from the keel, then lashes mast and keel together with an ox-thong and rides them on the winds.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XII / THE SIRENS, SCYLLA AND CHARYBDIS, THE CATTLE OF THE SUN. / BOOK XIII / ULYSSES LEAVES SCHERIA AND RETURNS TO ITHACA.; lines 5712-5817
occurrences.motif_label: Return voyage home
occurrences.basis: The book heading and narrated action present Ulysses leaving Scheria by ship and arriving near Ithaca.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses crosses the threshold; Alcinous sends a guide, Arete sends maidservants with clothing, a strong box, corn, and wine, and the crew puts these and other provisions aboard.

A rug and linen sheet are spread for Ulysses in the stern; the crew loosens the ship and rows out, while Ulysses falls into a deep, sweet, almost deathlike sleep; the ship travels swiftly over dark blue water.
At the appearance of the bright star before dawn, the ship draws near land.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XII / THE SIRENS, SCYLLA AND CHARYBDIS, THE CATTLE OF THE SUN. / BOOK XIII / ULYSSES LEAVES SCHERIA AND RETURNS TO ITHACA.; lines 5712-5817
occurrences.motif_label: Sheltered harbor as arrival threshold
occurrences.basis: The ship reaches Ithaca at dawn and the harbor is described as enclosed and protected from storms.

evidence.quote_or_summary: At the appearance of the bright star before dawn, the ship draws near land.
In Ithaca is the haven of the old merman Phorcys, enclosed by two points that shelter ships from wind and sea.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XII / THE SIRENS, SCYLLA AND CHARYBDIS, THE CATTLE OF THE SUN. / BOOK XIII / ULYSSES LEAVES SCHERIA AND RETURNS TO ITHACA.; lines 5819-5919
occurrences.motif_label: homecoming in sleep and nonrecognition
occurrences.basis: Ulysses is transported home while asleep, wakes on his own soil, and fails to recognize his native land because of long absence and divine fog.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The Phaeacians land the sleeping Ulysses with his bedding, place his gifts by the root of an olive tree away from the road, and depart.
Ulysses wakes on his own soil but does not know it; Minerva has made a foggy day to conceal his arrival and instruct him before recognition and revenge; the landscape appears changed to him.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: PREFACE TO SECOND EDITION / HENRY FESTING JONES. / THE ODYSSEY / BOOK I; lines 589-680
occurrences.motif_label: returning avenger restores threatened household
occurrences.basis: Minerva discusses whether Ulysses will return and take revenge in his own house, and frames the suitors' presence as destructive to the household.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Telemachus says the gods have hidden his father more closely than any mortal, that storm-winds carried him off without trace, and that suitors from Dulichium, Same, Zacynthus, and Ithaca are consuming his house while courting his mother.

Minerva says Ulysses is needed at home; if armed as when she first knew him, he would deal with the suitors quickly. She recalls his quest for arrow poison from Ilus and says the suitors would have a short shrift and sorry wedding.

Minerva says heaven will determine Ulysses' return, then advises Telemachus to call an assembly, order the suitors away, send Penelope to her father if she wants remarriage, sail with twenty men to Pylos and Sparta for news, perform rites and build a barrow if Ulysses is dead, and consider killing the suitors; she cites Orestes' fame for killing Aegisthus.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: PREFACE TO SECOND EDITION / HENRY FESTING JONES. / THE ODYSSEY / BOOK I; lines 589-680
occurrences.motif_label: painful song of return reopens grief for the absent husband
occurrences.basis: Phemius sings of the return from Troy; Penelope weeps and asks him to stop because the song reminds her of Ulysses.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Phemius sings to silent hearers about the sad return from Troy and the ills Minerva laid on the Achaeans. Penelope hears from upstairs, descends with two handmaids, stands by a bearing post, holds a veil before her face, and weeps.

Penelope asks Phemius to sing some other feat of gods and heroes and to stop the sad tale because it breaks her heart and reminds her of her lost husband, whose name was great over Hellas and middle Argos.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XII / THE SIRENS, SCYLLA AND CHARYBDIS, THE CATTLE OF THE SUN. / BOOK XIII / ULYSSES LEAVES SCHERIA AND RETURNS TO ITHACA.; lines 5921-5999
occurrences.motif_label: Return to home country under concealment
occurrences.basis: The passage centers on Ulysses’ arrival in Ithaca, recognition that it is his own country, and Minerva’s instruction to tell no one he has come home.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Minerva says the country is well known as Ithaca and describes it as rugged but fertile, with corn, wine, rain, dew, cattle, goats, timber, and never-failing water places.
Ulysses is glad to find himself in his own country but does not speak the truth and makes up a lying story.

Minerva says she has come to confer with Ulysses, help hide the treasure from the Phaeacians, warn him of troubles in his house, and instructs him to tell no one of his return and endure insolence silently.
Ulysses asks Minerva in her father’s name to tell the truth, saying he does not believe he is really back in Ithaca and asking whether he has truly returned to his own country.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XII / THE SIRENS, SCYLLA AND CHARYBDIS, THE CATTLE OF THE SUN. / BOOK XIII / ULYSSES LEAVES SCHERIA AND RETURNS TO ITHACA.; lines 6001-6093
occurrences.motif_label: Return to homeland after long wandering
occurrences.basis: The passage explicitly describes Ulysses' return after a long voyage and his joy at seeing his own land again.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Minerva describes Ulysses' shrewdness, says he returned safely but lost his men, notes Neptune's anger, and identifies the haven of Phorcys, the olive tree, the Naiad cave, the cavern of offerings, and mountain Neritum.
Minerva disperses the mist; Ulysses sees his land, rejoices, kisses the soil, lifts his hands, and prays to the Naiad nymphs with a promise of offerings.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XII / THE SIRENS, SCYLLA AND CHARYBDIS, THE CATTLE OF THE SUN. / BOOK XIII / ULYSSES LEAVES SCHERIA AND RETURNS TO ITHACA.; lines 6001-6093
occurrences.motif_label: Hero disguises identity before reclaiming household
occurrences.basis: Minerva disguises Ulysses so no human will know him before he goes among the suitors, wife, son, and loyal servant.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Minerva promises to stay attentive, predicts bloodshed among those consuming Ulysses' substance, and says she will disguise him so no human being will know him.
Minerva tells disguised Ulysses to go to the loyal swineherd near Raven rock and the fountain Arethusa while she goes to Sparta to see Telemachus with Menelaus.
Minerva touches Ulysses with her wand, wrinkles and withers his body, removes his yellow hair, blears his eyes, gives him filthy tattered clothing, a deer skin, a staff, and a holed wallet.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XII / THE SIRENS, SCYLLA AND CHARYBDIS, THE CATTLE OF THE SUN. / BOOK XIII / ULYSSES LEAVES SCHERIA AND RETURNS TO ITHACA.; lines 6001-6093
occurrences.motif_label: Threatened heir returning through ambush
occurrences.basis: Minerva reports that Telemachus is away and that suitors lie in wait at sea to kill him before he can return home.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses asks why Minerva did not tell Telemachus; Minerva answers that Telemachus is comfortable with Menelaus, while the suitors wait at sea to kill him before he returns, though she expects they will fail.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XIII / ULYSSES LEAVES SCHERIA AND RETURNS TO ITHACA. / BOOK XIV / ULYSSES IN THE HUT WITH EUMAEUS.; lines 6096-6194
occurrences.motif_label: return to homeland through humble threshold
occurrences.basis: Ulysses, newly in Ithaca, moves from the haven through a mountain route to the hut of his loyal swineherd rather than directly to a palace.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses leaves the haven, travels through wooded country over a mountain crest, and reaches the place where Minerva said he would find the swineherd.
The swineherd sits before his hut by pig yards he built in his master's absence; the passage details fences, sties, numerous pigs, fierce hounds, and boars consumed by the suitors.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XIII / ULYSSES LEAVES SCHERIA AND RETURNS TO ITHACA. / BOOK XIV / ULYSSES IN THE HUT WITH EUMAEUS.; lines 6196-6288
occurrences.motif_label: return of the absent lord with vengeance
occurrences.basis: The speech centers on the promised homecoming of Ulysses within the year and his vengeance on those harming his household.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses swears by king Jove, the rites of hospitality, and Ulysses' hearth that Ulysses will return within the year and take vengeance on those mistreating his wife and son; he refuses reward until this occurs.

Eumaeus says Ulysses will not come home, though Penelope, Laertes, Telemachus, and he wish it. He reports that Telemachus went to Pylos for news and that the suitors lie in wait for him, unless the son of Saturn protects him.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XIII / ULYSSES LEAVES SCHERIA AND RETURNS TO ITHACA. / BOOK XIV / ULYSSES IN THE HUT WITH EUMAEUS.; lines 6196-6288
occurrences.motif_label: unrecognized or self-concealing returner tells an alternate life story
occurrences.basis: Ulysses is present in the hut while speaking of Ulysses' return in the third person and then gives a detailed Cretan autobiographical account as the old stranger.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses swears by king Jove, the rites of hospitality, and Ulysses' hearth that Ulysses will return within the year and take vengeance on those mistreating his wife and son; he refuses reward until this occurs.

Ulysses begins by saying he could tell his sorrows for twelve months, then claims to be Cretan, son of Castor son of Hylax and a purchased slave concubine, once honored like legitimate brothers, later given little inheritance, enriched through marriage, and inclined to war, ships, weapons, ambushes, and foreign expeditions before Troy.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XIII / ULYSSES LEAVES SCHERIA AND RETURNS TO ITHACA. / BOOK XIV / ULYSSES IN THE HUT WITH EUMAEUS.; lines 6290-6372
occurrences.motif_label: homecoming after war and uncertain return
occurrences.basis: The speaker describes sailing home after Troy, and Pheidon reports that Ulysses seeks divine guidance on whether to return to Ithaca openly or secretly after long absence.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The speaker says he rose among the Cretans, led ships to Troy with Idomeneus, fought nine years, sacked Priam’s city, returned home briefly, then fitted out nine ships, sacrificed, feasted, and sailed from Crete toward Egypt.

Pheidon says he hosted Ulysses, shows Ulysses’ treasure, reports that Ulysses went to Dodona to learn Jove’s mind from the high oak about whether to return to Ithaca openly or secretly, swears a ship and crew were ready, and sends the speaker toward Dulichium.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XIII / ULYSSES LEAVES SCHERIA AND RETURNS TO ITHACA. / BOOK XIV / ULYSSES IN THE HUT WITH EUMAEUS.; lines 6374-6464
occurrences.motif_label: return of the absent master
occurrences.basis: Eumaeus discusses the absent master Ulysses, rejects reports, and later prays for Ulysses to return home.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Eumaeus says he doubts the stranger's claims about Ulysses, describes Ulysses as absent and carried away by storm winds, and notes that Penelope calls him when news about Ulysses arrives.

The swineherds bring in pigs for the night; Eumaeus orders the best pig sacrificed for the stranger, cuts firewood, has a five-year-old boar brought to the altar, throws facial bristles into the fire, and prays for Ulysses' return.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: ULYSSES LEAVES SCHERIA AND RETURNS TO ITHACA. / BOOK XIV / ULYSSES IN THE HUT WITH EUMAEUS. / BOOK XV; lines 6547-6648
occurrences.motif_label: divinely instructed return home
occurrences.basis: Minerva tells Telemachus to leave Lacedaemon, warns him of dangers at home and on the route, and gives instructions for his arrival in Ithaca.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Minerva goes to Lacedaemon, finds Telemachus sleepless, and tells him not to remain away from home because suitors threaten his property and his mother may be urged toward remarriage.

Minerva warns that suitors lie in wait in the strait between Ithaca and Samos, instructs Telemachus to sail night and day away from the islands, and tells him to go to the swineherd and send word to Penelope.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: ULYSSES LEAVES SCHERIA AND RETURNS TO ITHACA. / BOOK XIV / ULYSSES IN THE HUT WITH EUMAEUS. / BOOK XV; lines 6650-6731
occurrences.motif_label: bird omen of homecoming and revenge
occurrences.basis: An eagle carrying a white goose appears on the right and is interpreted by Helen as a sign that Ulysses will return after travel and suffering and take revenge on the suitors.

evidence.quote_or_summary: An eagle flies on the right, carrying a great white goose taken from a farmyard; people chase it shouting, and it passes close in front of the horses on the right.
Pisistratus asks Menelaus whether heaven sent the omen for the travelers or for Menelaus.

Helen says she will read the omen: as the eagle came from its mountain nest, so Ulysses, after far travel and suffering, will return to take revenge, or may already be back preparing harm for the suitors.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: ULYSSES LEAVES SCHERIA AND RETURNS TO ITHACA. / BOOK XIV / ULYSSES IN THE HUT WITH EUMAEUS. / BOOK XV; lines 6650-6731
occurrences.motif_label: urgent return home by ship
occurrences.basis: Telemachus asks to be brought directly to his ship because he must go home at once, and then orders his men to prepare the ship for departure.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Telemachus asks Pisistratus to leave him at his ship rather than take him to Nestor's house, saying he must go home at once.
Pisistratus decides to turn toward the ship, places Menelaus's gifts of gold and raiment in the stern, and urges Telemachus to board before Nestor can come fetch him.
Telemachus calls his men together and orders them to get everything ready on board the ship and set out home.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: ULYSSES LEAVES SCHERIA AND RETURNS TO ITHACA. / BOOK XIV / ULYSSES IN THE HUT WITH EUMAEUS. / BOOK XV; lines 6733-6832
occurrences.motif_label: return voyage under threat of death or capture
occurrences.basis: Telemachus directs the ship onward while wondering whether he will escape death or be taken prisoner.

evidence.quote_or_summary: After sunset and darkness, the vessel makes a quick passage onward, and Telemachus heads toward the flying islands while wondering whether he will escape death or be captured.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: PREFACE TO SECOND EDITION / HENRY FESTING JONES. / THE ODYSSEY / BOOK I; lines 682-759
occurrences.motif_label: failed or ill-fated return from war
occurrences.basis: Telemachus defends the bard’s song about the ill-fated return of the Danaans and notes that Ulysses was not the only man who did not return from Troy.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Telemachus tells his mother to let the bard sing, says Jove sends good and evil, mentions the ill-fated return of the Danaans and Ulysses not returning from Troy, then sends her to loom, distaff, servants, and declares himself master in the house.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: ULYSSES LEAVES SCHERIA AND RETURNS TO ITHACA. / BOOK XIV / ULYSSES IN THE HUT WITH EUMAEUS. / BOOK XV; lines 6834-6930
occurrences.motif_label: Return to parents used as lure and motive
occurrences.basis: The trader asks whether the woman wants to go with them to see her living parents, and she accepts if protected by oath.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The man who seduced her asks whether she wants to go with them to see her parents, who are alive and well off.
The woman says she will gladly go if the men swear a solemn oath that they will do her no harm by the way, and they swear as instructed.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: ULYSSES LEAVES SCHERIA AND RETURNS TO ITHACA. / BOOK XIV / ULYSSES IN THE HUT WITH EUMAEUS. / BOOK XV; lines 6932-7022
occurrences.motif_label: homecoming by sea and movement toward loyal household servant
occurrences.basis: Telemachus reaches Ithaca by ship, separates from the vessel, and heads to the swineherd's homestead.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Telemachus and his crew near land, lower sail and mast, row into harbor, moor the ship, go ashore, mix wine, and prepare dinner.
Telemachus tells the crew to take the ship to town while he remains to inspect herdsmen on one of his farms, promising them a dinner later.
Telemachus puts on sandals, takes a bronze-headed spear, the ship departs for the city, and he walks quickly to the swineherd's homestead.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: ULYSSES IN THE HUT WITH EUMAEUS. / BOOK XV / BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS.; lines 7025-7122
occurrences.motif_label: return of the absent son
occurrences.basis: Telemachus arrives after travel, and Eumaeus receives him with joy compared to a father welcoming an only son after ten years abroad and hardship.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Eumaeus reacts to Telemachus’ arrival by dropping wine bowls, kissing and embracing him, weeping for joy, and speaking as one who feared he would never see him again; the narration compares the joy to a father receiving a long-absent only son and says he embraced him as though he had come back from the dead.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: ULYSSES IN THE HUT WITH EUMAEUS. / BOOK XV / BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS.; lines 7025-7122
occurrences.motif_label: hidden lord witnesses disorder in his house
occurrences.basis: Ulysses, present as the stranger, hears of and condemns abuses in his own household and speaks of Ulysses or Ulysses’ son fighting there rather than enduring the disgrace.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses says he is shocked by the suitors’ insolence and declares that if he were as young as Telemachus, or were Ulysses himself, he would rather die fighting in his own house than see strangers mistreated, women servants dragged about, wine wasted, and bread consumed to no purpose.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: ULYSSES IN THE HUT WITH EUMAEUS. / BOOK XV / BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS.; lines 7124-7222
occurrences.motif_label: Return of the long-absent hero to his own country
occurrences.basis: Ulysses says he has come home to his own country in the twentieth year after long wandering and hardship.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses says no other Ulysses will come, identifies himself as the one returned in the twentieth year, and explains that Minerva can make him appear as a beggar or as a young man in good clothes.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: ULYSSES IN THE HUT WITH EUMAEUS. / BOOK XV / BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS.; lines 7124-7222
occurrences.motif_label: Recognition of a returned father by his son
occurrences.basis: Ulysses reveals himself as Telemachus' father after divine transformation, and father and son eventually embrace and weep.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses denies being a god, says he is Telemachus' father, kisses his son, and lets a tear fall from his cheek to the ground.
Telemachus says he cannot yet believe this is his father and argues that no mortal could make himself old and young so quickly unless a god were with him.
Ulysses says no other Ulysses will come, identifies himself as the one returned in the twentieth year, and explains that Minerva can make him appear as a beggar or as a young man in good clothes.
Telemachus throws his arms around his father; both weep loudly like eagles or vultures robbed of half-fledged young, and Telemachus asks what ship and crew brought Ulysses to Ithaca.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: ULYSSES IN THE HUT WITH EUMAEUS. / BOOK XV / BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS.; lines 7224-7319
occurrences.motif_label: concealed return to the homeland
occurrences.basis: Ulysses has been brought back to Ithaca, hides his gifts, keeps his identity secret, and plans to re-enter his house under disguise.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses says the Phaeacians escorted him over the sea to Ithaca while he slept, gave him bronze, gold, and raiment now concealed in a cave, and that he came on Minerva's suggestion to plan against their enemies.

Ulysses says the gods will not stay out of the fray, instructs Telemachus to return home, and says the swineherd will bring him disguised as a miserable old beggar; Telemachus must endure seeing him mistreated.
Ulysses tells Telemachus that no one must know he is in the house, not Laertes, Eumaeus, servants, or Penelope, and proposes testing the women and other servants.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: ULYSSES IN THE HUT WITH EUMAEUS. / BOOK XV / BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS.; lines 7321-7414
occurrences.motif_label: safe return despite ambush
occurrences.basis: Telemachus' ship arrives safely after the suitors had waited to capture and kill him, and Antinous says a god must have conveyed him home.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Amphinomus sees the ship inside the harbour and says they need not send a message because the ship is already there.
Antinous says the gods have saved Telemachus and that the suitors must make an end of him before he can call the Achaeans in assembly.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: ULYSSES IN THE HUT WITH EUMAEUS. / BOOK XV / BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS.; lines 7321-7414
occurrences.motif_label: divine disguise of the returning hero
occurrences.basis: Minerva changes Ulysses into an old man with a wand and clothes him in old garments to preserve his concealment after his return.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Eumaeus returns to Ulysses and Telemachus as they prepare supper after sacrificing a young pig; Minerva turns Ulysses into an old man with a stroke of her wand and clothes him in old garments so the swineherd will not recognize him or tell Penelope.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: ULYSSES IN THE HUT WITH EUMAEUS. / BOOK XV / BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS.; lines 7416-7431
occurrences.motif_label: return and hidden presence of a father
occurrences.basis: The passage identifies Telemachus's father as present and receiving a hidden smile, in the larger passage label context of Ulysses in the hut; the line itself presents the father as physically present but not openly acknowledged to Eumaeus.

evidence.quote_or_summary: “On hearing this Telemachus smiled to his father, but so that Eumaeus could not see him.”

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XV / BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII; lines 7434-7526
occurrences.motif_label: return to the household
occurrences.basis: Telemachus returns to his house and is emotionally received by Penelope, Euryclea, and the maids; Penelope also asks about the expected return of Ulysses.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Euryclea sees Telemachus, runs to him crying, and the maids come up and kiss his head and shoulders.
Penelope comes from her room looking like Diana or Venus, weeps, embraces Telemachus, kisses him, calls him the light of her eyes, and asks what he saw after going to Pylos.
Penelope sits opposite them by a bearing-post, spinning; after the meal she says she will return to her tear-watered couch and asks Telemachus whether he heard anything about Ulysses' return.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XV / BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII; lines 7434-7526
occurrences.motif_label: disguised or reduced-status hero as beggar-stranger
occurrences.basis: Ulysses is present under the social status of a stranger and beggar who will go into town seeking bread and drink.

evidence.quote_or_summary: At dawn Telemachus puts on sandals, takes a spear, says he will go to town to show himself to his mother, and tells the swineherd to take the unfortunate stranger to town to beg for drink and bread.
Ulysses says a beggar can do better in town, asks to be taken after warming by the fire, and notes that his thin clothes are inadequate for the frosty morning.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XV / BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII; lines 7528-7613
occurrences.motif_label: Return of the absent householder to confront usurpers
occurrences.basis: Menelaus frames the suitors as usurping Ulysses' bed and predicts their destruction if Ulysses returns; Theoclymenus says Ulysses is already in Ithaca preparing a reckoning.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Menelaus says the suitors would usurp a brave man's bed and compares them to young animals in a lion's lair; the returning lion will make short work of them, as Ulysses would of the suitors.

Theoclymenus tells Penelope he can divine surely, invokes Zeus, hospitality, and Ulysses' hearth, and says Ulysses is in Ithaca investigating evil deeds and preparing a day of reckoning; he cites an omen seen on the ship.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XV / BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII; lines 7528-7613
occurrences.motif_label: Disguised return in lowly appearance
occurrences.basis: Ulysses travels toward the city in rags, with a shabby wallet and staff, looking like a broken-down old tramp while his identity as master is known to the narration.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses throws a shabby tattered wallet over his shoulders, receives a stick from Eumaeus, and follows him in rags, looking like a broken-down old tramp leaning on a staff.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XV / BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII; lines 7615-7715
occurrences.motif_label: returning master arrives unrecognized at his own house
occurrences.basis: Ulysses reaches his own house in poor condition, is not publicly acknowledged as the master, and hears a prayer for his return while hostile figures deny it.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Melanthius mocks Ulysses as a miserable beggar, calls him unfit for honorable gifts or work, and says stools will be thrown at him if he approaches Ulysses' house.
Eumaeus prays to the fountain nymphs, children of Jove, that heaven may send Ulysses home to end the insults and bad shepherding of men like Melanthius.
Melanthius threatens to sell Eumaeus abroad and wishes Apollo or the suitors would kill Telemachus, adding that Ulysses will never come home.
Ulysses praises the house's size and defenses, including a surrounding battlemented wall and double doors, and notes the smell of roast meat and sound of music within.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XV / BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII; lines 7615-7715
occurrences.motif_label: abused disguised hero restrains vengeance
occurrences.basis: Ulysses is insulted and kicked, considers killing or beating Melanthius, but chooses endurance and self-control.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Melanthius mocks Ulysses as a miserable beggar, calls him unfit for honorable gifts or work, and says stools will be thrown at him if he approaches Ulysses' house.
Melanthius kicks Ulysses on the hip; Ulysses stands firm, considers retaliation, and decides to endure it and restrain himself.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XV / BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII; lines 7615-7715
occurrences.motif_label: loyal animal recognizes absent master
occurrences.basis: Argos, Ulysses' old dog, recognizes him when he comes to the house and dies after the recognition.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Argos, bred by Ulysses before Troy and formerly used for hunting, lies neglected on mule and cow dung heaps and is full of fleas.
Argos sees Ulysses, drops his ears, wags his tail, cannot approach, and Ulysses secretly wipes away a tear.
"Argos died as soon as he had recognised his master."

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XV / BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII; lines 7615-7715
occurrences.motif_label: household disorder during master's absence
occurrences.basis: The suitors feast in Ulysses' house, Melanthius joins them, and Eumaeus states that servants neglect work when the master's hand is absent.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Melanthius reaches the house, sits among the suitors opposite Eurymachus, and receives meat and bread from servants.
Ulysses praises the house's size and defenses, including a surrounding battlemented wall and double doors, and notes the smell of roast meat and sound of music within.
Eumaeus says Argos belonged to the man who died far away, recalls his former hunting excellence, and says servants neglect work when the master's hand is absent.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XV / BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII; lines 7615-7715
occurrences.motif_label: prayer for the absent ruler's return
occurrences.basis: Eumaeus prays to the fountain nymphs that heaven may send Ulysses home to end the insults of men like Melanthius.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Eumaeus prays to the fountain nymphs, children of Jove, that heaven may send Ulysses home to end the insults and bad shepherding of men like Melanthius.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XV / BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII; lines 7717-7818
occurrences.motif_label: Return in beggar appearance
occurrences.basis: Ulysses comes inside the house in the appearance of a poor old beggar and is treated as a stranger while present among Telemachus, Eumaeus, and the suitors.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses enters looking like a poor miserable old beggar, leaning on a staff, wearing rags, and sits on an ash-wood threshold by a cypress-wood bearing-post.
Telemachus takes bread and meat and tells Eumaeus to take it to the stranger and tell him to beg from the suitors.
After the suitors applaud the bard, Minerva prompts Ulysses to beg from each suitor so he may distinguish good from bad, while she will not save any of them.
Ulysses goes around from left to right, stretching out his hands as though a real beggar; some suitors pity him and ask who he is and where he came from.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XV / BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII; lines 7820-7923
occurrences.motif_label: Disguised returning lord abused in his own house
occurrences.basis: Ulysses, identified by the narration as Telemachus' father and Penelope's husband, appears as a poor stranger in the household and is insulted and struck by Antinous while his son and wife await revenge.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Antinous insults the beggar, orders him out, refuses food, and Ulysses replies that Antinous would not give a poor man salt or bread.
Antinous threatens Ulysses, throws a footstool, hits him on the right shoulder blade; Ulysses stands firm, silently broods on revenge, and sits at the threshold with his wallet.
Telemachus is furious about the blow to his father, sheds no tear, shakes his head in silence, and broods on revenge.

Penelope asks Eumaeus to call the stranger so she may ask about Ulysses; Eumaeus praises the stranger's tale and reports his claims of Cretan origin, friendship with Ulysses' house, and news that Ulysses is alive near the Thesprotians.
Penelope says the suitors waste the household's oxen, sheep, goats, and wine, and that if Ulysses came again, he and his son would soon have revenge.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XV / BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII; lines 7925-7968
occurrences.motif_label: awaited return of the absent husband
occurrences.basis: The interview is to concern the return of Penelope's husband, and Ulysses asks that Penelope wait until sundown to question him.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses tells Eumaeus he will speak truthfully to Penelope, fears the cruel suitors, reports being struck, and asks to wait until sundown to sit near the fire and answer questions about her husband's return.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII / BOOK XVIII; lines 7971-8072
occurrences.motif_label: disguised returner tested in his own house
occurrences.basis: Ulysses is in his own house but appears as an old ragged stranger; he must endure challenge and conceal his identity while acting within the household.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Book XVIII opens with a common tramp named Arnaeus, called Irus, who begs around Ithaca and insults Ulysses, trying to drive him from the doorway of his own house.
Ulysses girds up his old rags and exposes his powerful body; Minerva strengthens his limbs, the suitors are astonished, and Irus becomes frightened while servants bring him forward by force.

Ulysses decides to use a lighter blow so the Achaeans will not suspect who he is; Irus strikes his shoulder, and Ulysses strikes Irus under the ear, breaking skull bones and making blood gush from his mouth while the suitors laugh.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII / BOOK XVIII; lines 8074-8175
occurrences.motif_label: disguised returning husband among hostile suitors
occurrences.basis: Ulysses is present in the house as a poorly treated stranger while his speech says the dishonoured wife’s husband is certain to return soon and that the suitors will not part from him bloodlessly.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses puts a dirty tattered wallet over his shoulder, sits on the threshold, and is mocked by suitors who invoke the gods and threaten to send him to king Echetus.
Ulysses addresses Amphinomus, speaks of human vanity, divine changes of fortune, and warns that the suitors dishonour the wife and estate of one who will return soon, when bloodshed will follow.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII / BOOK XVIII; lines 8177-8277
occurrences.motif_label: disguised return to the household
occurrences.basis: The narrator names Ulysses while he remains in the hall as the stranger who has defeated Irus and offers menial service among the suitors.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Telemachus tells Penelope that the stranger defeated Irus and wishes Jove, Minerva, and Apollo would make all the suitors as helpless as Irus at the outer gate.
The narrator says Ulysses was glad to hear Penelope trying to get presents from the suitors and flattering them with fair words that he knew she did not mean.
Ulysses tells the maids, servants of long-absent Ulysses, to go to Penelope and says he will hold the light for the suitors, adding that he can endure much.
Ulysses scowls at Melantho, calls her a vixen, and threatens to tell Telemachus what she has said.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XVI / ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII / BOOK XVIII; lines 8279-8350
occurrences.motif_label: Unrecognized returner tested by insults in his own house
occurrences.basis: Ulysses is present in his own house as a stranger or beggar, is mocked by a suitor, and speaks of Ulysses coming to his own again.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Eurymachus addresses Ulysses as stranger, offers servant work building fences or planting trees, and accuses him of preferring begging to labor.
Ulysses challenges Eurymachus to compete in mowing, ploughing, and battle, calls him insolent and cruel, and warns that the doors will be narrow for the suitors if Ulysses returns.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII / BOOK XVIII / BOOK XIX; lines 8353-8450
occurrences.motif_label: hidden return of the householder
occurrences.basis: Ulysses is present in his own house as the stranger, remains unrecognized by Penelope and the maids in this passage, and secretly prepares action against the suitors.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses remains in the cloister planning, with Minerva’s help, to kill the suitors; he tells Telemachus to remove the armour and give excuses involving smoke and the danger of drunken quarrels over weapons.

Euryclea bolts the women inside; Ulysses and Telemachus move helmets, shields, and spears; Minerva precedes them with a gold lamp, and Telemachus sees the house glowing as if with fire and says some god has come down from heaven.

Ulysses replies to Melantho, describing his ragged begging state, claiming he was once rich before Jove took all away, and warning her that Ulysses may still come home and that Telemachus is grown enough to notice wrongdoing.
Penelope asks Eurynome to bring a fleece-covered seat for the stranger; after he sits, Penelope asks who he is, where he comes from, and who his parents are.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII / BOOK XVIII / BOOK XIX; lines 8452-8531
occurrences.motif_label: disguised returner under false identity
occurrences.basis: Ulysses is present as a stranger, avoids his true ancestry, and supplies a detailed alternate Cretan identity as Aethon.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses asks Penelope not to seek his race and family, saying such memories would increase his sorrow and that continual grieving in another's house is improper.
Penelope asks the stranger to tell who he is and where he comes from, saying he cannot be the son of an oak or a rock.

Ulysses replies with a Cretan identity tale: Crete is fertile, has ninety cities and many peoples; Cnossus was ruled by Minos, who conferred with Jove; Minos fathered Deucalion, whose sons were Idomeneus and the claimed Aethon.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: HENRY FESTING JONES. / THE ODYSSEY / BOOK I / BOOK II; lines 851-936
occurrences.motif_label: prophecy of the long-absent hero's return
occurrences.basis: Halitherses says Ulysses is close at hand and recalls his earlier prophecy that Ulysses would return in the twentieth year after hardship, loss of his men, and unrecognized arrival.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Halitherses, called the best prophet and omen-reader among them, says mischief is brewing for the suitors and that Ulysses is close at hand to deal out death and destruction.
Halitherses says he had foretold that Ulysses, after hardship and loss of all his men, would come home in the twentieth year unrecognized, and says this is coming true.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII / BOOK XVIII / BOOK XIX; lines 8533-8618
occurrences.motif_label: concealed homecoming and delayed recognition
occurrences.basis: Ulysses is physically beside Penelope while she treats him as a stranger; the conversation centers on whether and how Ulysses will return.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Penelope weeps as she listens, compared to snow thawing into water-filled rivers; Ulysses feels pity but restrains his tears while sitting beside her.
“I shall put you to the test... Tell me, then, how he was dressed, what kind of a man he was to look at, and so also with his companions.”
Ulysses says Ulysses is close at hand and swears by Jove and by Ulysses’ hearth that all he has said will come to pass, with Ulysses returning by the end of the moon and beginning of the next.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII / BOOK XVIII / BOOK XIX; lines 8620-8703
occurrences.motif_label: disguised return recognized by bodily mark
occurrences.basis: The returning master is present in disguise and is recognized by Euryclea through the scar on his leg during foot washing.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Euryclea prepares a cauldron with cold and hot water; Ulysses sits by the fire and turns from the light because he fears she will recognize a scar on his leg.
As Euryclea washes her master, she knows the scar from a wild boar wound received while hunting on Mt. Parnassus with Autolycus and his sons.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII / BOOK XVIII / BOOK XIX; lines 8705-8786
occurrences.motif_label: return of the long-wandering concealed hero
occurrences.basis: Ulysses states that he has come home after twenty years of wandering, while his identity remains hidden from most of the household.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Euryclea looks toward Penelope as if to tell her, but Minerva diverts Penelope’s attention. Ulysses restrains Euryclea and orders her not to reveal him, saying he has returned after twenty years of wandering and warning her of consequences if she speaks.

Ulysses tells Euryclea to keep silent and leave matters to heaven; she fetches more water, washes and anoints him, and Ulysses warms himself by the fire while hiding the scar under his rags before Penelope speaks.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS. / BOOK XVII / BOOK XVIII / BOOK XIX; lines 8788-8861
occurrences.motif_label: returning husband destroys suitors
occurrences.basis: The dream eagle identifies itself as the husband returned to bring the suitors to a disgraceful end, and Ulysses says the suitors’ death is portended.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The eagle says that the geese are the suitors and that it is Penelope’s own husband returned to bring them to a disgraceful end.
Ulysses replies that the dream has only one interpretation: Ulysses has shown how it will be fulfilled, and the suitors’ death is portended with none escaping.
Ulysses tells Penelope not to defer the tournament, because Ulysses will return before the suitors can string the bow and shoot through the iron.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XVII / BOOK XVIII / BOOK XIX / BOOK XX; lines 8864-8959
occurrences.motif_label: Returning hero in his own house before vengeance
occurrences.basis: Ulysses is identified as being in his own house with wife and son inside, while he plans how to kill the suitors occupying it.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses lies in the cloister on a bullock’s hide, sheep skins, and a cloak; he lies awake brooding on how to kill the suitors; laughing women leave the house after being with the suitors, provoking his anger.
Minerva comes down from heaven in the likeness of a woman, hovers over Ulysses, and tells him that he is in his own house and that his wife and son are safe inside.
Ulysses tells Minerva he doubts how he can kill the many suitors single-handed and asks where he could escape from their avengers after the deed.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XVII / BOOK XVIII / BOOK XIX / BOOK XX; lines 8961-9043
occurrences.motif_label: Unrecognized returnee tested by household responses
occurrences.basis: Ulysses is present in his own house but is repeatedly addressed as a stranger; household figures respond differently, including care from Euryclea and the swineherd, hostility from Melanthius, and pity from Philoetius.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The maids light the hearth fire. Telemachus arms himself and asks Euryclea about the stranger's bed and board; Euryclea says the stranger drank wine, declined more bread, refused bed and blankets, and slept on a bullock hide and sheepskins with a cloak.
Twenty women go to the fountain, others work in the house, attendants chop firewood, and the swineherd brings three pigs before asking Ulysses about the suitors' treatment of him.
Melanthius the goatherd arrives with goats for the suitors' dinner and two shepherds, ties the goats under the gatehouse, and insults Ulysses as a begging stranger.

Ulysses stays silent and broods. Philoetius arrives with a barren heifer and goats, asks the swineherd about the stranger, and says he looks like someone who had been a great man, while noting that the gods give sorrow even to kings.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XVII / BOOK XVIII / BOOK XIX / BOOK XX; lines 9045-9146
occurrences.motif_label: Return of the absent master with promised vengeance
occurrences.basis: Philoetius hopes for Ulysses’ return, and Ulysses swears that Ulysses will return and kill the suitors.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Philoetius greets the poor stranger, says he reminds him of Ulysses, laments the possibility that Ulysses is dead in Hades, describes the suitors consuming cattle and seeking Ulysses’ property, and says he still believes his master will return.
Ulysses tells the stockman he is sensible and swears by Jove and by Ulysses’ hearth that Ulysses will return before the stockman leaves and will kill the suitors.
The stockman says he would do his utmost to help if Jove brought this about, and Eumaeus similarly prays that Ulysses might return home.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XVII / BOOK XVIII / BOOK XIX / BOOK XX; lines 9045-9146
occurrences.motif_label: Loyal servants awaiting the rightful master
occurrences.basis: Philoetius remains attached to Ulysses despite hardship and says he would help him; Eumaeus prays for the return.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Philoetius greets the poor stranger, says he reminds him of Ulysses, laments the possibility that Ulysses is dead in Hades, describes the suitors consuming cattle and seeking Ulysses’ property, and says he still believes his master will return.
The stockman says he would do his utmost to help if Jove brought this about, and Eumaeus similarly prays that Ulysses might return home.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XVII / BOOK XVIII / BOOK XIX / BOOK XX; lines 9148-9215
occurrences.motif_label: returning father poised to punish offenders in his house
occurrences.basis: Telemachus watches his father, expecting him to begin an attack upon the suitors who are in Ulysses' house and have brought doom on themselves.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Theoclymenus says he has his own eyes, ears, feet, and understanding mind; he sees mischief overhanging those insulting and plotting ill in Ulysses' house, says none will escape, and goes back to Piraeus, who welcomes him.
“Telemachus gave him no heed, but sat silently watching his father, expecting every moment that he would begin his attack upon the suitors.”

The dinner had been abundant after many sacrifices, but the coming supper is described as gruesome, to be laid before the suitors by a goddess and a brave man because they had brought doom on themselves.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XVIII / BOOK XIX / BOOK XX / BOOK XXI; lines 9218-9315
occurrences.motif_label: Absent rightful owner's weapon returns as instrument of vengeance
occurrences.basis: The bow belongs to absent Ulysses, the suitors dishonour him in his own house, and the narrator foreshadows Antinous' death by Ulysses' arrows.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The bow's history is recounted: Iphitus and Ulysses meet while pursuing lost livestock; Iphitus gives Ulysses the bow, Ulysses gives a sword and spear in return, and Hercules later kills Iphitus as his guest and keeps the mares.
The narrator says Antinous expects to string the bow but will be the first to taste arrows from Ulysses, whom he is dishonouring in his own house.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XVIII / BOOK XIX / BOOK XX / BOOK XXI; lines 9317-9414
occurrences.motif_label: disguised return and private recognition
occurrences.basis: Ulysses privately tests two servants, reveals that he has returned in the twentieth year, and is recognized after showing his scar.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Outside the gates, Ulysses asks the stockman and swineherd whether they would support Ulysses or the suitors; the stockman and Eumaeus express longing for Ulysses’ return, after which Ulysses reveals himself and promises rewards if heaven delivers the suitors to him.

Ulysses shows the scar from a boar’s tooth received while hunting on Mt. Parnassus with the sons of Autolycus; after examining it, the two servants weep, embrace and kiss him, and he kisses their hands and faces.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: HENRY FESTING JONES. / THE ODYSSEY / BOOK I / BOOK II; lines 938-1036
occurrences.motif_label: restoration of household authority against predatory guests
occurrences.basis: The passage centers on the suitors consuming Ulysses’ estate, Telemachus’ challenge to them, and expectations surrounding Ulysses’ possible return.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Mentor says the Ithacans have forgotten Ulysses, who ruled like a father, and criticizes them for sitting still instead of stopping the suitors, though the people are many and the suitors few.
Leiocritus calls Mentor’s words folly, says one man cannot fight many over food, and claims Ulysses would have his own blood on his head if he fought the suitors against such odds.

Telemachus says he cannot eat or take pleasure with the suitors, accuses them of wasting his property while he was a boy, and says he will do them harm as far as he can, whether at home or by going to Pylos.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XVIII / BOOK XIX / BOOK XX / BOOK XXI; lines 9505-9596
occurrences.motif_label: returning hero reasserts strength in his own house
occurrences.basis: Ulysses is associated with absence, receives his own bow as a seeming stranger, proves he is still strong, and is joined by his son armed beside his seat.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses handles and examines the bow to see whether worms damaged its horns during his absence, while bystanders mock him as a tricky old bow-fancier.
Ulysses strings the bow as easily as a skilled bard strings a lyre; the string sings, the suitors are dismayed, and Jove thunders loudly as an omen.
Ulysses takes an arrow, draws it while seated, and shoots through all the axe handle-holes into the outer courtyard.
Ulysses tells Telemachus that the guest has not disgraced him, that he did not miss, that he is still strong, and that it is time for supper and song and dance.
Ulysses makes a sign with his eyebrows, and Telemachus arms himself with sword and spear beside his father's seat.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XIX / BOOK XX / BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII; lines 9599-9707
occurrences.motif_label: returning ruler punishes household usurpers
occurrences.basis: Ulysses explicitly identifies himself as returned from Troy and condemns the suitors for occupying his household, wooing his wife, wasting his goods, and plotting against his son and local authority.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses tells the suitors they thought he would not return from Troy, accuses them of wasting his goods, abusing women servants, wooing his wife, and fearing neither God nor man, and says they shall die.
Eurymachus addresses Ulysses, says Antinous led the wrongs, claims Antinous wanted to kill Telemachus and rule Ithaca, and offers fines in oxen, gold, and bronze.
Ulysses refuses any present or future goods and says he will not stay his hand until all the suitors are paid in full; they must fight or try to flee.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XIX / BOOK XX / BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII; lines 9599-9707
occurrences.motif_label: disguised hero reveals himself through decisive weapon use
occurrences.basis: Ulysses tears off his rags, stands with his bow and arrows, and begins killing the suitors after the contest has ended.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses tears off his rags, takes his bow and quiver, lays arrows at his feet, and says the contest is ended before aiming at another mark.
Ulysses shoots Antinous in the throat while Antinous holds a two-handled gold cup for wine; Antinous falls and blood flows.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XIX / BOOK XX / BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII; lines 9599-9707
occurrences.motif_label: father and son join in armed restoration of household
occurrences.basis: Telemachus kills an attacker, stands at his father's side, fetches armor, and arms himself and the loyal servants near Ulysses.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Amphinomus attacks Ulysses at the door, and Telemachus strikes him from behind with a spear before returning to his father's side.
Telemachus asks to bring armor, fetches four shields, eight spears, and four brass helmets, and arms himself, the swineherd, and the stockman near Ulysses.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XIX / BOOK XX / BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII; lines 9709-9805
occurrences.motif_label: reclaiming the household against armed usurpers
occurrences.basis: Ulysses fights armed suitors in his own house with his son and loyal allies, while opponents threaten to kill father and son and seize property.

evidence.quote_or_summary: After leaving Melanthius in cruel bondage, the allies arm themselves and return to Ulysses; four men stand in the cloister while the suitors remain many in the court.
The suitors raise an uproar; Agelaus warns Mentor not to side with Ulysses and threatens to kill him and absorb his property into Ulysses' property after father and son are killed.
Minerva, angered, scolds Ulysses by recalling his nine years fighting at Troy, his killings there, and the stratagem by which Priam's city was taken.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XIX / BOOK XX / BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII; lines 9807-9908
occurrences.motif_label: returning master punishes household usurpers
occurrences.basis: Ulysses is identified as acting in his own house against suitors who had sought his wife and harmed him during his absence.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Ulysses and his companions strike back: Ulysses hits Eurydamas and Agelaus, Telemachus hits Amphimedon and Leocritus, Eumaeus hits Polybus, and the stockman kills Ctesippus after taunting him.
Leiodes catches Ulysses' knees, asks for mercy, says he never wronged the women, tried to stop the others, and was the suitors' sacrificing priest.
Ulysses replies that as sacrificing priest Leiodes must have prayed against his return and for marriage to his wife; Ulysses then kills him with Agelaus' sword.

occurrences.source_title: The Odyssey
occurrences.passage_locator: BOOK XIX / BOOK XX / BOOK XXI / BOOK XXII; lines 9910-10015
occurrences.motif_label: returning householder restores violent order
occurrences.basis: Ulysses, identified as Telemachus’ father and Penelope’s husband, commands the post-slaughter restoration of his house, including punishment, cleanup, and purification.

evidence.quote_or_summary: A spared man asks that Ulysses be told not to kill him; Ulysses says Telemachus has saved his life and sends him and the bard outside while he finishes the slaughter.
Ulysses tells Telemachus, the stockman, and the swineherd to remove the dead, make the women help, clean the tables and seats with sponges and water, and then kill the women with swords.
The women carry out the dead bodies, clean the tables and seats with sponges and water, and carry away blood and dirt while Telemachus and the two others shovel it up.

After washing their hands and feet, Ulysses asks Euryclea to bring sulphur, which cleanses pollution, and fire so he may burn it and purify the cloisters; he also tells her to summon Penelope and the women.

occurrences.source_title: Phaedrus

occurrences.basis: The passage says the ideal is sought in Phaedrus and Phaedo as something to recover from a former state of existence.

evidence.quote_or_summary: The introduction connects Phaedrus with Symposium, says the two contain Plato's philosophy of love, joins love with philosophy, and describes an ideal sought as recovery from a former state of existence.

occurrences.source_title: Phaedrus
occurrences.passage_locator: Phaedrus / PHAEDRUS / INTRODUCTION.; lines 804-884
occurrences.motif_label: Return to origin after a cosmic cycle
occurrences.basis: The passage says that after ten thousand years all return to the place from which they came, though return is also tied to conduct across successive existences.

evidence.quote_or_summary: At the completion of ten thousand years all return to their place of origin, but the return is also represented as depending on good conduct in successive stages of existence.

occurrences.source_title: Phaedrus

occurrences.motif_label: returning dead or absent masters rebuke the present age
occurrences.basis: Michael Angelo and Shakespeare are hypothetically imagined as returning to earth and rebuking contemporary art and criticism.

evidence.quote_or_summary: Michael Angelo or Shakespeare are imagined returning to earth and courteously rebuking people for putting preliminaries of art in place of art and for seeking artificial effects rather than living creations.

occurrences.source_title: The Republic
